items.title: The ideal electrostatic conductor model
items.statement:
Under the Countable Choice convention of the stated boundary and sheet-distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]), Adopt as a physical model of ideal electrostatic conductors, for the classical laboratory framework of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: a **conductor configuration** consists of the following data, and every model of this postulate is required to satisfy the clauses below. No experiment is reported and no empirical value is inferred; this is an explicitly adopted equilibrium idealization together with its geometric and source conventions.
(a) [Geometry] a laboratory region $\Omega\times I$ with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ an arbitrary open ambient region, a finite family $D_1,\dots,D_m$ ($m\ge1$) of bounded $C^\infty$ domains with pairwise disjoint closures in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] with closures strictly inside $\Omega$ (the **conductor bodies**), the **conductor** $D:=D_1\cup\cdots\cup D_m$, its **surface** $\partial D$, and the **vacuum region** $\Omega_v:=\Omega\setminus\overline D$. By [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]], $\partial D=\partial D_1\cup\cdots\cup\partial D_m$ is a disjoint union of compact embedded $C^\infty$ hypersurfaces. The vacuum $\Omega_v$ is open, and near each conductor surface it is locally the smooth exterior side of that conductor. No boundedness or regularity of the ambient boundary is inferred from openness. In the additional **bounded smooth ambient branch**, assume that $\Omega$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain; only then [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]] gives that $\Omega_v$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with the specified outer/conductor boundary charts; we additionally require $\Omega_v$ to be connected (configurations whose vacuum region is separated by the conductors, for instance by an enclosing closed shell, are outside this model as formulated here).
(b) [Equilibrium and sources] the configuration is in the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] on the vacuum region: $B=0$, $J=0$, $E$ is the fixed-time electric field of [[def-em-fields]], the volume source density $\rho_v$ is a continuous real map on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (C m$^{-3}$, [[def-em-sources]]) extended by zero to $D$; the **conductor charge is a stationary surface charge**, i.e. a continuous density $\sigma:\partial D\to\mathbb R$ (C m$^{-2}$) whose pairing with test functions is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with tangential current $K=0$ and $S=\partial D$; and the field pair $(E,0)$ together with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},\ 0)$ satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]. Inside the conductor the field vanishes: $E\equiv0$ on $D$ (the **equilibrium condition**); equivalently the conductor interior is field-free and carries no volume charge.
(c) [Potential and equipotential convention] there is a function $\varphi\in C^0(\Omega)\cap C^2(\Omega_v)$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ and with $\varphi$ constant on each conductor body, $\varphi|_{D_j}\equiv V_j$ for real constants $V_j$ (volts, [[def-em-si-conventions]]); by continuity of $\varphi$ the trace of $\varphi$ on each $\partial D_j$ from the vacuum side equals $V_j$ as well. This is the single-function convention of an ideal conductor with no double layer: the model reads the same potential value on both sides of $\partial D$, while the normal component of $E$ may jump.
(d) [Data] a model is completed either by the component potentials $V_1,\dots,V_m$ together with the volume source $\rho_v$ and the data on $\partial\Omega$ where the laboratory region is bounded, or by the component total charges $Q_j:=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS$ (C) together with those same ambient data. These are two declared data types; the postulate asserts neither that both data types are simultaneously specifiable nor that either is solvable for arbitrary data.
(e) [Scope] This is a static, frame-relative equilibrium idealization: it excludes transient finite-conductivity dynamics, relaxation to equilibrium, moving surface charge, electrode polarization and contact effects, and it is not derived from a microscopic matter model. It asserts no existence or uniqueness theorem (those are separate conditional results), no force, no energy, no radiation, no measurement and no apparatus realization; the value $V_j$ is a model parameter and the surface density $\sigma$ is an idealization variable determined by the equilibrium problem when it is solvable. The general open ambient branch retains compact conductor bodies in exterior configurations. Its additional bounded smooth ambient branch is distinct from the separately declared grounded-half-space and infinite parallel-plane idealizations, whose conductor bodies are themselves noncompact. Those examples retain the equilibrium/equipotential interpretation but their noncompact bodies and plane distributions are not instances of this compact-body configuration or its compact-sheet predicate. No arbitrary exterior solvability is asserted.
items.strategy: Nonproof formulation and scope review: adopt the equilibrium objects already defined in the framework and record their exact interfaces instead of proving a physical law. Textbook conductor treatments support each clause as a model choice: the vanishing interior field with all charge on the surface and the constant potential of an equipotential conductor ([[def-em-weak-sources]]'s stationary-sheet source is the framework's own surface-distribution object), the grounded/fixed-potential and fixed-charge data distinction, and the idealization's limits are stated rather than hidden. The mathematical identities used to name the objects are exact: $\partial D$ is a finite disjoint union of compact embedded smooth hypersurfaces by [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]. For general open $\Omega$, removing the finite compact separated closures gives an open vacuum, with smooth local exterior conductor charts because each compact body is strictly inside $\Omega$ and separated from the others. The vacuum need not be bounded or have a smooth outer boundary. Only under the additionally imposed bounded $C^\infty$ ambient hypothesis does [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]] give a bounded smooth vacuum; the surface pairing $\sigma\delta_{\partial D}$ is the one of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) under the surface-distribution conventions of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] and carries its declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]); the field, source and regime objects are those of [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]] and [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]; and the adopted solution predicate is [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], not a consequence of the smooth postulate. The clause (d) data distinction is a definitional choice (Dirichlet data $V_j$ versus charge data $Q_j$), and clause (e) states the exclusions; in particular no claim is made that a configuration exists for arbitrary data, and no empirical or metrological content is attached to the idealization.

items.physical_scope: The ideal electrostatic conductor idealization of the classical framework in one named inertial frame: finitely many compact smooth field-free conductor bodies inside a general open laboratory region, with a separate bounded smooth ambient branch, all conductor charge carried by continuous stationary surface densities, a connected vacuum region in which the pure electrostatic regime and the adopted distributional Maxwell equations hold, and a continuous equilibrium potential that is constant on each conductor body and continuous across its surface. The item is a model choice: it asserts no existence, uniqueness, dynamics, conductivity, forces, energy, radiation, measurement or apparatus claim, and it excludes cavity configurations with disconnected vacuum regions.

items.title: Surface charge and normal field on an ideal conductor
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) inherited from the surface and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v;E;\rho_v;\sigma;V_j)$ be a model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] with surface $S:=\partial D$ and vacuum region $\Omega_v$, with the fields of [[def-em-fields]], the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] carried by the model, and suppose additionally that the field $E$ satisfies the joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity hypothesis of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]] across $S$: around every $x_0\in S$ each side of $S$ is the restriction of a $C^1$ field on an open neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller graph chart. Let $n$ denote the unit normal on $S$ pointing from the conductor side into the vacuum side (equivalently: $n$ is the inward normal of $\Omega_v$ and the outward normal of $D$ on $S$, by the local exterior conductor chart; in the bounded smooth ambient branch this is the sign convention of [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c)), and let $E_+$ denote the vacuum-side trace of $E$ (the field is zero on the conductor side, so $[E]=E_+$). Then, pointwise on $S$:
(a) [Normal sheet charge] $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $n\times E_+=0$; equivalently $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+$ and the tangential part of the vacuum-side field vanishes: $E_+$ has no component tangent to $S$. In particular a conductor surface with $\sigma=0$ at a point has $E_+=0$ there (both traces vanish), and the sign of $\sigma$ is the sign of the outward normal field component.
(b) [Normal derivative of the potential] with $\varphi$ the model's potential and $\partial\varphi/\partial n:=\nabla\varphi_+\cdot n$ the one-sided normal derivative in the direction $n$ from the conductor into the vacuum ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]]), one has
$$\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial n}=-\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sigma=-\varepsilon_0\,\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial n}.$$
(c) [Equipotential boundary traces] the trace $\varphi_+$ of $\varphi$ on $S$ is constant on each connected component of $S$, with value $V_j$ on every connected component contained in $\partial D_j$; consequently the boundary value problem in the vacuum region is a Dirichlet problem whose data are the constants $V_j$ on the conductor surfaces.
(d) [Total charges] the total charge of conductor $j$ is
$$Q_j=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}n\cdot E_+\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\nu}\,dS,$$
where $\nu$ is the local outward normal of the vacuum along the smooth conductor interface $S$, without asserting regularity of a general ambient outer boundary (so $\nu=-n$ on $\partial D$ and the last equality uses $\partial\varphi/\partial\nu=-\partial\varphi/\partial n$); the surface integrals exist as integrals of continuous functions over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]).
(e) [Data reading] the two data types of the model are related through (d): if the component potentials and ambient data are fixed and the equilibrium solution is given, the total charges are determined by (d); prescribing the total charges instead determines the potentials only through the (separate) equilibrium problem, and this theorem asserts no existence or uniqueness for charge data.
(f) [Scope] The statement is pointwise and stationary: it assumes the one-sided joint regularity above, a $C^\infty$ conductor surface, and the pure electrostatic regime; it excludes moving surface charge, normal sheet currents, magnetic sheet sources, nonsmooth or cornered conductors, fields without one-sided traces, forces, energy and any measurement; no self-force or material response is asserted.
items.strategy:
The model supplies $E\equiv0$ on the conductor side and the source pair $(ho_v+\sigma\delta_S,0)$ with $K=0$ as the stationary-sheet pairing of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c), and [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] supplies the adopted weak Maxwell equations; the joint one-sided regularity is the hypothesis of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]]. Applying that theorem with $\Omega_-$ the conductor side, $\Omega_+$ the vacuum side and the chosen normal $n$ (its sign convention is exactly the one of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] fixed in the model) gives, pointwise on $S$, $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $n	imes[E]=0$ together with the two magnetic identities. Since $E\equiv0$ on the conductor side, $[E]=E_+-0=E_+$, proving (a) and the formula $\sigma=\varepsilon_0n\cdot E_+$. For (b): on the vacuum side $E=-
abla\varphi$ by the model, and $\varphi$ is $C^2$ in the vacuum interior, is continuous on $S$, and its gradient has the continuous one-sided trace $-E_+$ by the admitted field regularity; the parallel-graph derivative argument below identifies the actual tangential derivatives of the trace; hence $n\cdot E_+=-n\cdot
abla\varphi_+=-\partial\varphi/\partial n$ with the classical normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]], and substituting into (a) gives the stated sign. For (c): $n	imes E_+=0$ says precisely that all tangential first derivatives of $\varphi_+$ vanish at every point of $S$; the trace $t\mapsto\varphi_+(t)$ is therefore locally constant on the embedded hypersurface $S$, and a locally constant continuous function on a connected component is constant there ([[def-connected-component-and-quasicomponent]]; in each graph chart the trace has zero gradient, so [[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]] makes it constant on the chart, and local constancy on a connected set gives constancy on the whole component). On a component contained in $\partial D_j$ the model's continuity convention gives the value $V_j$ ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]](c)). For (d): the total charge is the surface integral of $\sigma$, which exists because $\sigma$ is continuous on the compact $S$ and the surface measure is finite ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]); substituting (a) gives the middle expression, and the last equality is $
u=-n$ and $\partial\varphi/\partial
u=
abla\varphi_+\cdot
u=-
abla\varphi_+\cdot n=-\partial\varphi/\partial n$, with the local exterior-side vacuum normal, agreeing with [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c) whenever its additional bounded ambient hypothesis holds. No product of distributions is formed, no equation at a corner is asserted, and the result is exactly the pointwise form of the conductor boundary condition under the stated regularity. The potential's gradient trace needed in (b)-(c) is justified by the field trace: $
abla\varphi=-E$ in the vacuum, so its first derivatives extend continuously to the boundary by $-E_+$. In a graph chart, restrict $\varphi$ to parallel graphs inside the vacuum. On a compact coordinate segment their derivatives are $-E\cdot\partial_yX_s$ and converge uniformly to $-E_+\cdot\partial_yX_0$ as $s\downarrow0$; the functions converge to the continuous boundary trace. [[thm-uniform-derivative-limit-on-a-closed-interval]] proves that this is the actual derivative of the trace, so constancy of the trace and tangential-field cancellation are legitimate without assuming an unprovided ambient extension of the potential.

items.physical_scope: The ideal-conductor boundary conditions of classical electrostatics in a named inertial frame: for a stationary smooth conductor surface in the pure electrostatic regime and fields with the stated one-sided regularity, the surface charge density equals epsilon_0 times the normal vacuum-side field, the vacuum-side field is normal to the surface, the potential trace is constant on each connected piece of the conductor surface with the model's component value, and the total component charges are the outward flux integrals of the vacuum field. The statement is conditional and pointwise; it excludes moving or nonsmooth surfaces, magnetic and current sources, forces, energy, material response and any empirical claim.

items.title: Uniqueness and flux compatibility for the electrostatic boundary value problem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited weak-solvability and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be continuous on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (the fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]), and let $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in C^2(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be real potentials of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields $E_i:=-\nabla\varphi_i$ of [[def-em-fields]] and
$$-\Delta\varphi_i=\rho/\varepsilon_0\qquad\text{pointwise on }\Omega_v,\qquad \Delta=\operatorname{div}\nabla.$$ The Laplacian convention is [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].
Let $\nu$ denote the outward unit normal of $\Omega_v$ ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]]). Then:
(a) [Classical Dirichlet uniqueness] if $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$, and hence $E_1=E_2$. The conclusion holds component by component; each connected component of a bounded $C^\infty$ domain is again a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, to which the connected-domain uniqueness corollary applies.
(b) [Classical Neumann uniqueness and compatibility] if $\partial_\nu\varphi_1=\partial_\nu\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$, then $\varphi_1-\varphi_2$ is constant on each connected component of $\Omega_v$, and conversely adding one real constant per component to a solution preserves both the equation and the Neumann data; hence the field $E$ is unique while the potential is determined only up to componentwise constants. Moreover the Neumann data are necessarily compatible:
$$\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\rho\,dx+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega_v^{(j)}}\partial_\nu\varphi\,dS=0\qquad\text{for every connected component }\Omega_v^{(j)}.$$
This compatibility is necessary, not sufficient, and is exactly the flux identity of the divergence theorem for the Poisson equation.
(c) [Weak variants] (i) if $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega_v)$ ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]) is prescribed as a trace and $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ are weak solutions of the Dirichlet problem with the same trace $g$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$; (ii) if the conormal data are prescribed compatibly, weak $H^1$ solutions are unique modulo constants on each connected component, and for connected $\Omega_v$ this is the normalised solution of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; (iii) [sheet/transmission variant] for the finite disjoint smooth interfaces and outer Dirichlet data of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c), the globally $H^1$ solution is unique, and for compatible outer Neumann data it is unique modulo componentwise constants until the componentwise means are fixed.
(d) [Physics reading and conductor case] on a star-shaped vacuum domain the curl-free $C^1$ field has an interior $C^2$ potential by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]]. This alone does not supply closure regularity, $H^1$ membership, a trace, or prescribed boundary data; each application of (a)-(c) additionally requires its stated regularity and identical boundary/source data. In the bounded conductor model, prescribed absolute conductor potentials $V_j$ and absolute outer Dirichlet data determine the potential and field uniquely in the admitted classical or weak class. Grounding fixes the additive constant exactly. If only relative potential differences are prescribed and the outer/reference data are also allowed to shift by the same constant, the common gauge constant is free; merely omitting outer boundary data does not establish field uniqueness.
(e) [Scope] uniqueness is conditional on the stated boundary or decay data: on an unbounded exterior region without a decay condition uniqueness fails: on $\Omega_R=\{x:|x|>R\}$ the functions $0$ and $u(x)=1-R/|x|$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity (the witness is verified in the strategy), so the boundary, decay and regularity hypotheses above cannot be dropped. No existence is inferred from uniqueness; the classical branch requires $C^2$ up to the closure, the weak branches carry their own domain, coefficient and trace hypotheses, and no dielectric material coefficient or empirical claim is included. For the admitted conductor class with connected vacuum, fixed absolute conductor potentials and identical outer Neumann data also give exact uniqueness: this is a mixed boundary problem with a nonempty Dirichlet part, so there is no surviving additive constant. Existence for those mixed data is not asserted here. In that weak mixed branch, write $\mathcal V_D=\{v\in H^1(\Omega_v):Tv=0\text{ on }\partial D\}$. The compared potentials have the same prescribed conductor trace and satisfy $\varepsilon_0\int_{\Omega_v}\nabla v\cdot\nabla\varphi=\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for every $v\in\mathcal V_D$, with the same smooth outer normal datum $g$.
items.strategy:
All four statements are read off their suppliers, with the physics conventions made explicit. (a) On each connected component $U$ of $\Omega_v$, the restricted potentials are $C^2(\overline U)$ with equal Laplacians $ho/\varepsilon_0$ and equal boundary traces, so the classical Dirichlet corollary ([[cor-classical-dirichlet-and-poisson-problems-are-unique]] claim 1) gives equality on $\overline U$; components are bounded by [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] and inherit the smooth-domain property as in [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](d). The fields then agree because $E_i=-
abla\varphi_i$ and the gradient is determined by the potential. (b) The same corollary's second claim ([[cor-neumann-solutions-are-unique-modulo-componentwise-constants]]) gives constancy of $\varphi_1-\varphi_2$ on each component from equal normal derivatives. The compatibility identity is [[lem-neumann-compatibility-from-the-divergence-theorem]] applied to $u=\varphi$, $f=-\Delta\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $g=\partial_
u\varphi$; its conclusion $\int f=-\int g$ is the displayed equation, and the source notes of that lemma record that it is necessary rather than sufficient. (c) (i) is the uniqueness clause of [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]] (the weak solution with prescribed trace is exactly one); (ii) is the uniqueness-modulo-constants and normalisation clause of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]] with the trace spaces of [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]; (iii) is [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c) verbatim in its uniqueness clause: outer Dirichlet data give the globally $H^1$ solution uniquely, outer compatible Neumann data give uniqueness modulo componentwise constants until the means are fixed. (d) The radial Poincare construction provides $\varphi\in C^2(\Omega_v)$ in the interior only. Before invoking (a), require the asserted continuous derivatives through order two on the closure and matching classical traces; before invoking (c), require $H^1$ membership, the specified trace/conormal problem, and matching weak right-hand sides. These are independent data/regularity hypotheses. Under the conductor Dirichlet data, the differences of admitted solutions have zero trace on every conductor and the prescribed outer boundary, so (a) or (c)(i) gives zero difference, not an unfixed constant. A common gauge shift preserves a relative-potential problem only when every reference datum is shifted as well. (e) For the failure of uniqueness on unbounded regions, put $\Omega_R:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|>R\}$ and $u(x):=1-R/|x|$; then $u\in C^\infty(\Omega_R)$, $u=0$ on $\{|x|=R\}$, $0<u<1$ on $\Omega_R$ and $u(x)	o1$ as $|x|	o\infty$, while $\Delta u=0$ because $R/|x|$ is the constant $4\pi R$ times the $n=3$ fundamental solution, harmonic off the origin ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]]) with the constant multiple and the constant function having zero Laplacian by linearity ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); hence $0$ and $u$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity, so the boundary/decay hypotheses in (a)-(c) cannot be dropped. No existence statement is made anywhere: the existence clauses are the separate declared existence result of this page and the cited weak-solvability lemmas, and the compatibility identity is used only in its necessary direction. For the mixed conductor data mentioned in (d), let $w$ be the difference of two admitted solutions. It is harmonic, $w=0$ on the conductor boundary and $\partial_
u w=0$ on the outer boundary. Green's first identity gives $\int_{\Omega_v}|
abla w|^2=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}w\partial_
u w=0$ because each boundary piece has one zero factor. Thus $w$ is constant on the connected vacuum and its zero trace on the nonempty conductor boundary makes that constant zero. For admitted weak mixed solutions, their difference has zero conductor trace, is an admissible test of the homogeneous mixed difference equation, and the same zero-energy argument applies. This conditional uniqueness requires the displayed boundary/trace class and does not supply a mixed existence theorem. In the weak mixed case the mean-zero inequality [[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]] turns $
abla w=0$ into $w=w_{\Omega_v}$ as an $H^1$ class. Its constant trace on the nonempty conductor boundary is zero, so the constant is zero; no classical differentiability of a general $H^1$ representative is assumed.

items.physical_scope: Uniqueness for the classical and weak Dirichlet/Neumann electrostatic boundary value problems in a bounded vacuum region of a named inertial frame, with the componentwise Neumann freedom, the necessary flux compatibility, and the conductor-potential reading: identical complete Dirichlet data determine the potential and field exactly; compatible Neumann data determine the field and leave one potential constant per connected component until a normalization is fixed. The statement is conditional on the stated boundary, decay and regularity data and on the cited mathematical suppliers; it asserts no existence, no arbitrary-boundary solvability, no material interfaces beyond the declared sheet branch, and no empirical claim.

items.title: Existence and regularity for the electrostatic boundary value problem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited solvability theorem ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be smooth on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]) and let $\varepsilon_0>0$ be the framework constant. Then the electrostatic boundary value problems on $\Omega_v$ are solvable in the following exact senses, and the solutions are the fields of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with volume source $\rho$:
(a) [Dirichlet branch] for every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ there is exactly one $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with
$$-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0\quad\text{on }\Omega_v,\qquad \varphi|_{\partial\Omega_v}=g,$$
with $\Delta$ the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]];
and it is the unique weak $H^1$ solution with trace $g$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the class); the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ ([[def-em-fields]]) is $C^\infty$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ and $(E,0)$ realises the pure electrostatic regime with source $\rho$ on the vacuum region.
(b) [Neumann branch] for every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ with
$$\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\rho\,dx+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega_v^{(j)}}g\,dS=0\qquad\text{for every connected component }\Omega_v^{(j)}\text{ of }\Omega_v,$$
there is $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $\partial_\nu\varphi=g$ (outward normal $\nu$, [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]), unique up to one additive constant per connected component; the normalisation $\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\varphi\,dx=0$ for every $j$ selects exactly one. The compatibility is also necessary in the sense of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b).
(c) [Conductor reading and surface-charge realization] for the separated compact-body conductor geometry and zero-interior-volume convention of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], additionally assuming $\Omega$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ ambient domain, with outer boundary data $g_0\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ on $\partial\Omega$ and constants $V_j$ on the conductor surfaces $\partial D_j$ (constant functions are smooth on the compact disjoint boundary pieces), the combined datum is a special case of (a); the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ extended by $E:=0$ on the conductor satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},\,0)$, where $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+\in C^\infty(\partial D)$ is the constructed continuous surface-charge density, agreeing afterwards with [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]] ([[def-em-weak-sources]](c), [[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]]); the total charges $Q_j=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}n\cdot E_+\,dS$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]) are thereby determined by the data, and $\varphi$ is constant on each $\partial D_j$ with value $V_j$.
(d) [Stationary sheet charge in the vacuum region] for finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces $\Gamma$ strictly inside $\Omega_v$, a smooth sheet density $\sigma_\Gamma$ on them, and outer Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$, there is a weak solution $\varphi\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ which is $C^\infty$ on the closure of each side of every $\Gamma$, unique by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](c)(iii), solving the weak equation with right-hand side $\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma_\Gamma\,Tv$; its flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon_0\nabla\varphi]=-\sigma_\Gamma$, equivalently $n\cdot[E]=\sigma_\Gamma/\varepsilon_0$ in the sign convention of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]]. This is the vacuum ($\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0$) transmission branch; no dielectric coefficient is introduced.
(e) [Scope] all existence statements are the ones proved in [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] for its stated smooth bounded domains, smooth uniformly positive coefficients (here $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$), smooth data and finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces; the coefficient is the smooth positive constant $\varepsilon_0I$ on every side in the transmission clause. Excluded: nonsmooth boundaries, corners, edges, coefficient loss of regularity, prescribed total charges for conductor bodies (the free equipotential problem), unbounded exterior regions without a stated decay class, dielectric material response (belonging to the material-response page) and any measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The theorem asserts existence of the potential, not of a physical equilibrium; the ideal conductor is the adopted model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]].
items.strategy:
The conductor application in (c) explicitly uses the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch, not the general open ambient model. The proof is a careful application of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] to the vacuum geometry, combined with the framework's distributional reading.
(a) Take $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$, which is smooth on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ and uniformly positive; the theorem's clause (a) gives exactly one weak solution with trace $g$, $C^\infty$ on the closure, with $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon_0
abla\varphi)=-\varepsilon_0\Delta\varphi=ho$ pointwise and the prescribed boundary values. Dividing by $\varepsilon_0>0$ gives the displayed equation; the field $E=-
abla\varphi$ is $C^\infty$ with $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=0$, so the static reduction of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](c) holds with $\partial_t=0$ and the pair $(E,0)$ is a pure electrostatic model. (b) The theorem's clause (b) with conormal datum $\varepsilon_0g$, since $
u\cdot\varepsilon_0
abla\varphi=\varepsilon_0\partial_
u\varphi=\varepsilon_0g$ gives a weak solution exactly under the displayed compatibility, unique modulo componentwise constants, normalised by the mean conditions; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure is the same clause. On each connected component, the weak identity tested with the constant $1$ reproduces the compatibility, matching [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b). (c) The datum that is $g_0$ on $\partial\Omega$ and $V_j$ on $\partial D_j$ is a function on the disjoint union $\partial\Omega_v=\partial\Omega\sqcup\partial D$ restricting to a smooth function on each piece, hence smooth on the boundary manifold; clause (a) applies with this $g$ and gives $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi=ho_v/\varepsilon_0$ (the volume source is $ho_v$). Define $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0 n\cdot E_+\in C^\infty(\partial D)$; the solution has constant trace $V_j$ on $\partial D_j$ because it solves the Dirichlet problem. Extend the potential by the constant $V_j$ inside $D_j$; the resulting function is continuous across each boundary. The tangential derivatives of the vacuum trace are zero: pull back the smooth up-to-boundary solution to a boundary graph and use the chain rule (or the uniform derivative-limit argument for parallel interior graphs). Therefore $E_+\cdot	au=-\partial_	au\varphi=0$ for every tangent vector $	au$, and $n	imes E_+=0$ is derived directly from the boundary datum. The density is defined by the displayed normal trace, before using any theorem that assumes a completed conductor model. Extend the field by zero on $D$ and let $\widetilde E$ denote the extension; on the open sets $\Omega_v$ and $D$ it is respectively $C^\infty$ and zero, so it has $C^\infty$ one-sided traces across the compact embedded interface $\partial D$ with normal $n$, and [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] gives, distributionally, $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=\{\operatorname{div}\widetilde E\}_{	ext{piecewise}}+n\cdot[\widetilde E]\,\delta_{S}$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=\{\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E\}_{	ext{piecewise}}+n	imes[\widetilde E]\,\delta_S$ with $S=\partial D$. The piecewise divergence is $ho_v/\varepsilon_0$ on $\Omega_v$ and $0$ on $D$; the piecewise curl is zero on both sides; $[\widetilde E]=E_+$ and $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n	imes E_+=0$ by the constant-trace argument just proved. Hence $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=(ho_v+\sigma\delta_S)/\varepsilon_0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega)$, with the sheet pairing of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) and the surface conventions of [[def-em-surface-distribution]]; together with $B=0$ and $J=0$ these are the four adopted equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] on the (time-independent) laboratory region, by the static dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]. The total charges follow by integrating the continuous density over the compact hypersurfaces ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]). (d) This is [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c) with the constant coefficient $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$, piecewise smooth bulk data and smooth sheet charge; the equal one-sided traces, one-sided smoothness and the jump sign are as stated there, and the identification with the framework's jump convention is [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]] ($n$ from the minus to the plus side). (e) records the exact hypotheses and the exclusions; no existence claim is made beyond the cited theorem, and in particular the free charge-data conductor problem and the exterior problem are left open. The extended potential, the zero interior field, the constructed sheet density and the verified distributional equations now satisfy the bounded conductor model; only after this construction may [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]] be invoked as a consequence. For (d) the coefficient form is explicitly $\varepsilon_0\int
abla v\cdot
abla\varphi=\intho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma_\Gamma Tv$; hence bulk and sheet data are not multiplied by $\varepsilon_0$, whereas a prescribed outward normal datum $g$ corresponds to conormal datum $\varepsilon_0g$. Both the sheet jump and all source factors follow from this same form.

items.physical_scope: Existence and uniqueness of the classical and weak electrostatic boundary value problems on a bounded smooth vacuum region of a named inertial frame: smooth Dirichlet data, compatible smooth Neumann data, and the conductor reading in which constant potentials on compact conductor surfaces together with outer boundary data determine the field and the induced surface charges and total charges. The transmission clause covers finite disjoint smooth interfaces with prescribed sheet charge in vacuum. The statement is conditional on the cited smooth solvability theorem and asserts no existence for prescribed total charges, no nonsmooth geometry, no dielectric material response, no unbounded exterior problem and no empirical claim.

items.title: The image-method certificate for a point charge above a grounded plane
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) inherited from the Newtonian, polar and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$$H:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:x_3>0\},\qquad \Pi:=\{x_3=0\},\qquad p:=a e_3\ (a>0),$$
let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a charge parameter (coulombs) and $\varepsilon_0>0$ the framework constant ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Define, with arbitrary values on the exceptional sets,
$$\varphi_I(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac1{|x-p|}-\frac1{|x+ae_3|}\right)\quad(x\in H\setminus\{p\}),\qquad E_I:=-\nabla\varphi_I.$$ The map $E_I$ is a spatial field of [[def-em-fields]] in the fixed-time reading, with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].
Then:
(a) [Candidate field] $\varphi_I\in C^\infty(H\setminus\{p\})$ and $\Delta\varphi_I=0$ pointwise on $H\setminus\{p\}$: the first term is the Coulomb potential of $p$, whose $n=3$ fundamental solution is harmonic off its pole ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]], [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d)), and the second term is $C^\infty$ and harmonic on the whole of $H$ because its pole $-ae_3$ lies outside $H$; $E_I$ is $C^\infty$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$.
(b) [Distributional point source] $\varphi_I\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$ and
$$-\Delta T_{\varphi_I}=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\,\delta_p\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(H),$$
where $T_{\varphi_I}$ is the regular distribution of $\varphi_I$ ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $\delta_p$ the Dirac distribution at $p$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); moreover the field satisfies $\operatorname{div}E_I=(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$ and $\operatorname{curl}E_I=0$ in $\mathcal D'(H)$, where the divergence and curl of $E_I$ are the distributional derivatives of its components ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). Thus $(E_I,0)$ is a pure electrostatic model on $H$ with the fixed-time point source $q\delta_p$, the static reading of the stationary point charge of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e)).
(c) [Boundary trace and decay] $\varphi_I$ extends continuously to $\overline H\setminus\{p\}$ with $\varphi_I=0$ on $\Pi$ (the two denominators are equal there), and for $|x|\ge2a$ the cancellation bound holds:
$$|\varphi_I(x)|\le\frac{2|q|\,a}{\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2}.$$
The bound follows by applying the mean value theorem along the segment from $-ae_3$ to $ae_3$ to the function $y\mapsto|x-y|^{-1}$, whose gradient is bounded by $(|x|-a)^{-2}$ there ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). In particular $\varphi_I(x)\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in $H$.
(d) [Uniqueness in the declared class] let $\psi:H\setminus\{p\}\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ and harmonic on $H\setminus\{p\}$, continuous on $\overline H\setminus\{p\}$, with $\psi=0$ on $\Pi$, $|x-p|(\psi(x)-\varphi_I(x))\to0$ as $x\to p$ and $\psi(x)\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in $H$. Then $\psi=\varphi_I$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$. Equivalently, the Dirichlet problem $\Delta\psi=0$ on $H\setminus\{p\}$, $\psi=0$ on $\Pi$, with the leading singularity of the point charge at $p$ and decay at infinity, has exactly one solution in the stated class.
(e) [Physics reading: ideal grounded plane in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]] the ideal grounded conducting half-space $\{x_3<0\}$ with the field $E_I$ on $H$, $E\equiv0$ below $\Pi$ and the induced density $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+|_\Pi=-\varepsilon_0\,\partial_3\varphi_I|_\Pi$ (using the normal $n=e_3$ from the conductor into the vacuum; $\sigma\in C^\infty(\Pi)$) is a model of the same equilibrium structure as [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]]: it is a pure electrostatic field on $H$ with the point source at $p$ and the equipotential boundary condition $\varphi_I=0$ on $\Pi$; the pair $(E_I,0)$ satisfies the static electrostatic equations with source $q\delta_p$ on $H$, and the induced density is explicitly $\sigma(x_1,x_2)=-qa/[2\pi(x_1^2+x_2^2+a^2)^{3/2}]$, is absolutely integrable over the plane, and has total charge $\int_\Pi\sigma\,dS=-q$. However, the half-space conductor is not a compact conductor body: the plane is not a compact embedded hypersurface, $\Pi$ and $\{x_3<0\}$ are not among the geometric objects of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], the density $\sigma$ is not a declared stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c), and the noncompact plane pairing is not an adopted compact-sheet source of that definition. As a separately specified mathematical idealization, extending $E_I$ by zero below the plane gives $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=(q\delta_p+\sigma\delta_\Pi)/\varepsilon_0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=0$ on $\mathbb R^3$, where $(\sigma\delta_\Pi)(\eta)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\sigma(x')\eta(x',0)dx'$. This verified identity does not extend the framework postulate to arbitrary noncompact sheets. The clause is the explicitly declared idealization whose exact mathematical content is (a)-(d).
(f) [Scope] the statement concerns the ideal point charge above an ideal grounded plane in the declared decay class; it excludes finite-plane edge effects, conductor thickness, transients, moving charges, radiation, self-force and any measurement; no uniqueness is asserted outside the class of (d), and the point-source singularity is never evaluated.
items.strategy:
(a) $|x-p|^{-1}$ is the $n=3$ fundamental solution kernel, harmonic off its pole, and $|x+ae_3|^{-1}$ is $C^\infty$ on $H$ because $|x+ae_3|\ge a>0$ there; sums of harmonic functions are harmonic by linearity of second derivatives ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and $
abla\varphi_I$ is computed off the pole by the chain and power rules ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). (b) Local integrability: $|x-p|^{-1}$ is locally integrable in dimension three and $|x+ae_3|^{-1}$ is continuous, so both have locally integrable components and the sum does (measurability is [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]) ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); the identification with regular distributions is [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]] and [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]. The distributional Laplacian of the first term is $(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and hence on the open subset $H$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d), [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), while the second term $u(x):=-(q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0))|x+ae_3|^{-1}$ is $C^\infty$ on $H$ with $\Delta u=0$ classically; for every compactly supported test $\eta\in\mathcal D(H)$ and every coordinate interval containing its support, [[thm-integration-by-parts]] gives $\langle\partial_iT_u,\etaangle=-\int u\,\partial_i\eta=\int(\partial_iu)\eta$, so $\partial_iT_u=T_{\partial_iu}$; applying the same identity to the $C^\infty$ function $\partial_iu$ gives $\partial_i\partial_iT_u=T_{\partial_i\partial_iu}$, and summing gives $\Delta T_u=T_{\Delta u}=0$ as the regular distribution of the zero function ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). The field is exactly the difference of the two point fields $E_q^p-E_q^{-p}$ restricted to $H$. Each component of the first field is locally integrable and represents $-\partial_iT_{\varphi_q^p}$ by [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d), not merely by potential integrability; the second point field is smooth on $H$ and satisfies the same identity there. Thus every field component is locally integrable, $T_{E_{I,i}}=-\partial_iT_{\varphi_I}$, and the divergence and curl identities follow from the point-field supplier and [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]. The first and second pole kernels and their gradients have radial absolute integrals $2\pi b^2$ and $4\pi b$ on radius-$b$ balls, respectively, by [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], confirming local integrability. The reading of $q\delta_p$ as the fixed-time point source is the dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e) and [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) on the half-space; the pair $(E_I,0)$ is then a pure electrostatic model there. (c) On $\Pi$ the two distances $|x-p|$ and $|x+ae_3|$ are equal, so the bracket vanishes; continuity on $\overline H\setminus\{p\}$ is continuity of the two kernels away from their poles. For the bound, write $f(y):=|x-y|^{-1}$ and apply the mean value theorem to $f$ on the segment from $-ae_3$ to $ae_3$: $|f(ae_3)-f(-ae_3)|\le 2a\sup_{|y|\le a}|
abla f(y)|$ with $|
abla f(y)|=|x-y|^{-2}\le(|x|-a)^{-2}$ ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]); for $r=|x|\ge2a$ the gradient is at most $4/r^2$, so the endpoint difference is at most $(2a)(4/r^2)=8a/r^2$; multiplication by $|q|/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$ gives exactly the displayed bound $2|q|a/(\pi\varepsilon_0r^2)$. (d) Apply [[lem-em-half-space-harmonic-uniqueness-with-decay]] to $w=\psi-\varphi_I$: both terms are $C^2$ harmonic on $H\setminus\{p\}$ and continuous on $\overline H\setminus\{p\}$, the trace on $\Pi$ vanishes because both do, and the difference has sub-Coulomb growth at $p$ and tends to zero at infinity by the bound of (c) and the hypothesis on $\psi$. The lemma yields $w=0$. (e)-(f) record the reading and scope: the geometric and source-theoretic exclusions are exactly those of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] and [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) (noncompact plane), The additional full-space plane identity is proved below as a separate mathematical idealization, without changing those physical source-type exclusions. The choice cost is the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the cited integral and distribution interfaces. Differentiate the two smooth kernels at $x_3=0$: $\partial_3\varphi_I=q a/[2\pi\varepsilon_0(r^2+a^2)^{3/2}]$, $r^2=x_1^2+x_2^2$, and tangential derivatives vanish since the boundary potential is identically zero. Hence $\sigma=-qa/[2\pi(r^2+a^2)^{3/2}]$, smooth even at $r=0$. Plane polar integration gives $\int_\Pi|\sigma|=|q|a\int_0^\infty r(r^2+a^2)^{-3/2}dr=|q|$ and $\int_\Pi\sigma=-q$, using the primitive $-(r^2+a^2)^{-1/2}$ on finite intervals, [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] and monotone convergence. Thus the sheet pairing is an order-zero distribution bounded by $|q|\|\eta\|_\infty$. For the full-space identity set $R=\widetilde E-E_q^p$. In $H$ it equals $-E_q^{-p}$ and below the plane it equals $-E_q^p$; both pieces are smooth through their closed half-spaces, with zero classical divergence and curl. For a compact test, coordinate integration by parts and Fubini give $\partial_iT_{R_j}=T_{\{\partial_iR_j\}}+\delta_{i3}[R_j]\delta_\Pi$: all products are absolutely integrable because the fields and derivatives are bounded on the compact half-space pieces and the test has bounded compact support. Tangential boundary terms vanish and the two vertical endpoint terms give the displayed jump. Here $[R]=E_q^p-E_q^{-p}=E_I|_\Pi$, whose normal component is $\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and tangential component is zero. Adding the full-space point-field identities yields precisely the asserted divergence and zero curl of $\widetilde E$. The product integrands are Borel; the exact product-measure identification and finite continuous integral comparison are [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] and [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. This noncompact-plane calculation is a local test identity, not a use of the compact-sheet physical postulate. For $q=0$ every field, potential and induced charge vanishes. The plane has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero by [[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]], so values assigned to the field on it do not change regular distributions. On $H$, the point-source physical reading uses the separate adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] for the stationary point source. Its four pairings hold by the computed spatial identities and the static dictionary. This adoption on the declared point-source class is distinct from the merely mathematical noncompact-plane pairing on all of $\mathbb R^3$.

items.physical_scope: The ideal electrostatic problem of a point charge held above an infinite grounded conducting plane, read in the framework's SI conventions: on the vacuum half-space the image potential is harmonic off the source, has the point-charge distributional source, vanishes on the plane, decays like |x|^-2, and is unique in the stated continuous-boundary and decay class; the plane's induced density is the idealization's bookkeeping normal-derivative reading. The item asserts no finite-plane edge effects, no conductor thickness, no dynamics, no self-force and no measurement, and the half-space conductor and noncompact sheet are explicitly outside the bounded-conductor model and the declared source types. The induced density is explicitly smooth on the whole plane, has absolutely convergent total charge $-q$, and the full-space point-plus-plane divergence identity is verified with local tests as a separate mathematical idealization. Matching singularities allow any remainder of order $o(|x-p|^{-1})$.

items.title: Capacitance and energy for specified linear conductor geometry
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the cited unit-Dirichlet solvability and trace interfaces, and its Countable Choice consequence for surface and integral interfaces ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v)$ be the conductor geometry of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], additionally with $\Omega$ a bounded $C^\infty$ ambient domain and $\Omega_v$ connected and with the **outer boundary $\partial\Omega$ grounded**: the data on $\partial\Omega$ are the constant Dirichlet datum $0$; let $\rho_v\equiv0$ on $\Omega_v$ (the pure capacitor configuration: no volume source), and let the framework constants be those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. For each $j\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ let $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be the unit-potential solution of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c) with the smooth data
$$\varphi_j|_{\partial D_k}=\delta_{jk},\qquad \varphi_j|_{\partial\Omega}=0,$$
so that $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ on $\Omega_v$ with the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and let $\nu$ be the outward normal of $\Omega_v$ (so on $\partial D_j$ the normal $\nu$ points into the conductor). Define the **capacitance matrix** by
$$C_{jk}:=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi_k}{\partial\nu}\,dS,\qquad j,k=1,\dots,m,$$
the flux integrals of continuous functions over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ (normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]) ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]]). Then:
(a) [Linearity and matrix form] for every $V=(V_1,\dots,V_m)\in\mathbb R^m$ the unique equilibrium potential with conductor potentials $V$ and grounded outer boundary is $\varphi^V=\sum_{j=1}^mV_j\varphi_j$, and the conductor charges of [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d) are
$$Q_j(V)=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi^V}{\partial\nu}\,dS=\sum_{k=1}^mC_{jk}V_k,\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad Q=CV.$$
(b) [Reciprocity] $C$ is symmetric: $C_{jk}=C_{kj}$ for all $j,k$; the symmetry is Green's symmetric pairing of the harmonic potentials $\varphi_j,\varphi_k$.
(c) [Energy identity] the field energy of the configuration is
$$U(V)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\Omega_v}|\nabla\varphi^V|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12V^{T}CV=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^mV_jQ_j(V),$$
and $U(V)>0$ for every $V\ne0$: $C$ is symmetric positive definite. In particular $U(V)\ge0$, with equality exactly for $V=0$, so every nonzero conductor-potential data set stores positive field energy.
(d) [Two-conductor reading] with only conductor $1$ driven and every other conductor grounded, $V=te_1$: $Q_1=C_{11}t$, $Q_j=C_{j1}t$ for $j\ne1$, and $U=\tfrac12C_{11}t^2=\tfrac12Q_1V_1=Q_1^2/(2C_{11})$; the **capacitance of the arrangement** at conductor $1$ with respect to the grounded reference is the positive geometric number $C_{11}>0$, with $C_{11}=Q_1/V_1$ when $t=V_1\ne0$, and the energy identities $U=\tfrac12QV=Q^2/(2C)=\tfrac12CV^2$ hold with $C=C_{11}$, $Q=Q_1$, $V=V_1$. By (c) the positivity holds for every diagonal entry, $C_{jj}>0$.
(e) [Assembly reading] use the family $V_j(s)=sV_j$, $\varphi_s=s\varphi^V$, $Q_j(s)=sQ_j(V)$ for $0\le s\le1$, with fixed geometry and grounded reference. Prescribe the quasistatic external charge-transfer work by $dW_{\rm ext}=\sum_jV_j(s)dQ_j(s)$. Then $W_{\rm ext}=\int_0^1s\,ds\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)=U$. The potentials vary during assembly; only the final potentials and geometry are fixed. This derives the sheet-charge accounting directly and does not apply the volume-source theorem [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] to singular sheets. The family is an accounting prescription, not an asserted time-dependent Maxwell/material solution.
(f) [Scope] the theorem assumes: the compact separated conductor geometry, the additional bounded smooth ambient domain, and connected vacuum region of the model, the grounded outer boundary $\partial\Omega$, zero volume source, and the existence and uniqueness of the unit-potential Dirichlet solutions ([[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c), [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](a)). It asserts no solvability for arbitrary boundary data (the existence theorem is used only for the constant data above), no prescribed-total-charge problem, no dielectric or material response, no finite-conductivity or transient charging dynamics, no radiation, and no measurement; the matrix $C$ is a geometric object of the ideal electrostatic model, and the ideal parallel-plate and similar formulas are statements about this model only.
items.strategy:
Use the additional bounded smooth ambient hypothesis with the separated compact body closures to obtain a bounded smooth vacuum by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]]. The general open ambient branch alone supplies no bounded Dirichlet solver. Existence of each $\varphi_j$: the pure electrostatic regime is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields [[def-em-fields]]; the datum that is $\delta_{jk}$ on $\partial D_k$ and $0$ on $\partial\Omega$ is constant, hence smooth, on each compact boundary piece of the disjoint union $\partial\Omega_v$, so [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c) gives $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ and those boundary values. (a) Linearity: $\sum_jV_j\varphi_j$ is a $C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ function with $-\Delta igl(\sum_jV_j\varphi_j igr)=0$ and boundary values $V_k$ on $\partial D_k$, $0$ on $\partial\Omega$; by the Dirichlet uniqueness of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](a) it is the unique equilibrium potential with those data, and the charges are obtained by substituting into the flux formula of [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d): the integral is linear in $\varphi$, giving $Q_j(V)=\sum_kC_{jk}V_k$. (b) Green's first identity on the bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega_v$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], applied twice and subtracted) gives, for the harmonic $\varphi_j,\varphi_k$,
$$0=\int_{\Omega_v} igl(\varphi_j\Delta\varphi_k-\varphi_k\Delta\varphi_j igr)d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial\Omega_v} igl(\varphi_j\partial_
u\varphi_k-\varphi_k\partial_
u\varphi_j igr)dS;$$
the outer boundary contributes zero because both potentials vanish there, and on the conductor surfaces $\varphi_j=\delta_{j\ell}$, so the sum over components $D_\ell$ reduces to $\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_
u\varphi_k-\int_{\partial D_k}\partial_
u\varphi_j$, i.e. $C_{jk}=C_{kj}$ after multiplying by $\varepsilon_0$. (c) Apply Green's first identity once more with $u=v=\varphi^V$:
$$\int_{\Omega_v} igl(\varphi^V\Delta\varphi^V+|
abla\varphi^V|^2 igr)d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}\varphi^V\partial_
u\varphi^V\,dS.$$
The Laplacian term vanishes, the outer boundary contributes $0$, and on $\partial D_j$ the trace of $\varphi^V$ is the constant $V_j$, so the boundary integral equals $\sum_jV_j\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_
u\varphi^VdS=\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)/\varepsilon_0$ by [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d); multiplying by $\varepsilon_0/2$ gives $U(V)=	frac12V^TCV$. Positivity: $
abla\varphi^V$ is continuous on the compact $\overline{\Omega_v}$, hence Borel and bounded, and $|
abla\varphi^V|^2$ is integrable with finite integral ([[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]); $U(V)\ge0$ because the integrand is nonnegative. If $U(V)=0$ then $\int|
abla\varphi^V|^2=0$, hence $
abla\varphi^V=0$ $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere by [[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]], hence $
abla\varphi^V=0$ everywhere by continuity, hence $\varphi^V$ is constant on the connected open set $\Omega_v$ ([[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]]); the constant is $0$ because $\varphi^V=0$ on the nonempty boundary $\partial\Omega$ and $\varphi^V$ is continuous on the closure; finally $V_j=\varphi^V|_{\partial D_j}=0$ for every $j$. Thus $C$ is positive definite and in particular symmetric with positive diagonal. (d) is the case $V=te_1$ of (a) and (c): $Q_1=C_{11}t$, $U=	frac12C_{11}t^2=	frac12Q_1V_1$, and eliminating $t=Q_1/C_{11}$ gives $U=Q_1^2/(2C_{11})$; $C_{11}>0$ is (c) with $V=e_1$. (e) Linearity gives $\varphi_s=s\varphi^V$, $V(s)=sV$, $Q(s)=sQ(V)$ and hence the surface density scales by $s$. Moving an infinitesimal charge $dQ_j$ from the grounded reference at zero potential to conductor $j$ has electric-force work $-V_j(s)dQ_j$, so the balancing quasistatic external contribution is $+V_j(s)dQ_j$. Prescribing this charge-transfer accounting and summing gives $\sum_jV_j(s)dQ_j(s)=s\,ds\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)$. Integrate $s$ from zero to one to obtain $W_{m ext}=	frac12\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)=U$. All signs of charges and voltages are admitted. The reference is grounded throughout but the driven potentials vary with $s$; external support is assumed. This is derived for the surface charges and not imported from the smooth volume-source hypothesis of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]]. (f) lists the hypotheses: only constant boundary data are solved, so no claim of arbitrary-boundary solvability or of charge-data solvability is made, and no material, radiative or empirical content is introduced. For (d), handle $t=0$ first: $\varphi^V=0$, all charges vanish and $U=0$, while $C_{11}$ is still defined by its unit-potential flux and is strictly positive. Only for $t
e0$ is the ratio $Q_1/V_1$ formed. Full AC is inherited solely through the unit Dirichlet/trace solvability suppliers; all subsequent finite linearity and energy calculations add no stronger assumption. The continuous nonnegative energy density can vanish almost everywhere only by vanishing everywhere in the open vacuum: a nonzero value would stay bounded below on a small Euclidean ball of positive measure ([[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). The endpoint work calculation uses the known global potential directly: [[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]] gives $\int_\gamma E_s\cdot dr=\varphi_s({m start})-\varphi_s({m end})$ on each interior piecewise $C^1$ path, and boundary endpoints are limits using the continuous closure traces. It does not apply the star-shaped existence hypotheses of the earlier electrostatic-work theorem to a conductor vacuum with holes. The charge-transfer family is prescribed bookkeeping, and no actual particle/source dynamics is inferred.

items.title: Force on a held charge above a grounded plane in the image model
items.statement:
Assume the Countable Choice convention of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]] and [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] ([[def-countable-choice]]). In the ideal grounded-plane configuration of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]]: vacuum half-space $H=\{x_3>0\}$, point charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ at $p=ae_3$ ($a>0$), field $E_I$ given by the image potential, and $E_I$ has the Coulomb singularity $(q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0))(x-p)/|x-p|^3$ of the source charge as $x\to p$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d), [[def-em-fields]]). Split the field near $p$ as
$$E_I(x)=E_q(x)+E_{\rm ext}(x),\qquad E_q(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{x-p}{|x-p|^3}\quad(x\ne p),$$
the **self-field** $E_q$ of the source charge and the **external (mirror) field** $E_{\rm ext}:=E_I-E_q$, which is $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $p$ (it is minus the gradient of the smooth mirror term $-q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)|x+ae_3|^{-1}$). Then:
(a) [External field at the charge] the external field at the location of the charge is
$$E_{\rm ext}(p)=-\frac{q}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}\,e_3 .$$
It is the gradient of the mirror term evaluated at $p$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).
(b) [Force on the held charge] under the adopted external Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i) at zero velocity, a test particle of charge $q$ held at $p$ experiences the electric force
$$F=q\,E_{\rm ext}(p)=-\frac{q^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}\,e_3,$$
strictly attractive toward the plane when $q\ne0$ and zero when $q=0$, of magnitude $q^2/(16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$; the particle's own field is excluded from the coupling by the postulate, so the result is a two-body-style external force of the mirror field and is not a self-force.
(c) [Reading and scope] for either nonzero sign of $q$ the force is attractive (the magnitude depends on $q^2$), while $q=0$ gives zero force; the induced total plane charge is $-q$ and its distribution is concentrated under the charge; the example is the exact ideal-model result for a held point charge, an ideal grounded plane and the adopted static external force law. It asserts no measurement, no dynamics of the charge (no motion or radiation), no finite-plane or finite-conductor correction, no self-force and no claim that the pair of idealisations is realised by an apparatus; the source is the idealised stationary point charge of [[pthm-em-image-method-certificate]](e), not a declared compact-source model. Here the displayed force is the electric contribution at rest. Holding the charge at $p$ requires a balancing support force $F_{\rm support}=-F$; the held trajectory is not asserted to solve the equation with the electric Lorentz force as its sole force.
items.strategy:
Both $E_I$ and $E_q$ are gradients off $p$; subtracting, $E_{m ext}=-
abla u$ with $u(x):=-\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{1}{|x+ae_3|}$, which is $C^\infty$ on the ball $|x-p|<a$ because $|x+ae_3|\ge a>0$ there ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Differentiating $u$ by the chain and power rules gives $
abla u(x)=+\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{x+ae_3}{|x+ae_3|^3}$ for $x$ in that ball; at $x=p=ae_3$ this is $\dfrac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{2ae_3}{(2a)^3}=\dfrac{q\,e_3}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}$, and $E_{m ext}(p)=-
abla u(p)=-\dfrac{q}{16\pi\varepsilon_0a^2}e_3$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). This proves (a). For (b): [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i) adopts the covariant equation of motion with the prescribed external field and explicitly excludes the particle's own field; at zero coordinate velocity the magnetic term vanishes and the coordinate force is $q$ times the external electric field, so the displayed force follows by substituting (a) ([[def-em-si-conventions]] fixes the units, N). The magnitude and attraction statements are immediate from the formula and $q^2\ge0$ with equality only for $q=0$, in which case there is no charge and no force. Clause (c) records the idealization: the total induced charge $-q$ is the induced-charge normalisation of the ideal plane recorded with the certificate, and nothing dynamical, radiative, measured or finite-geometry is claimed. In the adopted tensor convention [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], an instantaneous rest state has $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $U_0=-c$, so the spatial electric four-force components are $qF^{i0}U_0=q(-E_i/c)(-c)=qE_i$; $dt/d	au=1$ at rest identifies these with coordinate-force components. This is the electric contribution. The holding support supplies the opposite force, rather than requiring a constant trajectory to satisfy the sole-force equation. The certificate's explicit plane density integrates to $-q$ and supplies the induced-charge assertion; for $q
e0$ its absolute density is largest under the charge and decreases with transverse radius.

items.physical_scope: The external electrostatic force on an ideal point charge held at height a above an ideal grounded conducting plane, within the declared image model: the mirror field at the charge is -(q/(16 pi epsilon_0 a^2)) e_3 and the adopted external Lorentz coupling gives the attractive force -(q^2/(16 pi epsilon_0 a^2)) e_3 with self-field excluded. The item asserts no measurement, no motion, no radiation, no finite-geometry fringe corrections and no self-force. The attraction is strict for $q\ne0$ and the force vanishes for $q=0$; holding the charge requires the opposite support force. This is the electric contribution at rest, not a sole-force trajectory solution.

items.title: The ideal infinite parallel-plate capacitor
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the integral and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). **Declare the ideal parallel-plate model** of two infinite parallel charged planes in vacuo, read as equipotential ideal conductor surfaces of the same equilibrium structure as [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] (the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields [[def-em-fields]]): for a separation parameter $d>0$, half-separation $h=d/2$, a surface-density parameter $\sigma>0$ (C m$^{-2}$) and the framework constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the model consists of the field
$$E(x):=\begin{cases}-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}e_3,&|x_3|<h,\\[2pt]0,&|x_3|>h,\end{cases}\qquad x=(x_1,x_2,x_3),$$
together with the plane densities $+\sigma$ on $\Pi_+:=\{x_3=h\}$ and $-\sigma$ on $\Pi_-:=\{x_3=-h\}$, and with the piecewise potential $\varphi(x):=+\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}x_3$ for $|x_3|\le h$, $\varphi:=+\dfrac{\sigma h}{\varepsilon_0}$ for $x_3\ge h$ and $\varphi:=-\dfrac{\sigma h}{\varepsilon_0}$ for $x_3\le-h$. Then:
(a) [Direct distributional verification] $E$ and $\varphi$ are locally integrable and $C^\infty$ off $\Pi_+\cup\Pi_-$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ there, $\varphi$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$ and constant on each plane with the values $\varphi|_{\Pi_+}=+\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$, $\varphi|_{\Pi_-}=-\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$; and in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$
$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\bigl(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,$$
where $\delta_{\Pi_\pm}(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\psi(x_1,x_2,\pm h)\,dx_1\,dx_2$ for compactly supported smooth $\psi$ are the plane distributions defined by the iterated Lebesgue integrals. Equivalently, the model realises the static electrostatic equations with the declared pair of plane densities and no other source, and the potential differences read off $\varphi$ are $\varphi(h)-\varphi(-h)=2\sigma h/\varepsilon_0=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$.
(b) [Uniform field and voltage] the field between the planes has constant magnitude $|E|=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and is normal to the planes, and the potential difference between the plates is $V:=\varphi|_{\Pi_+}-\varphi|_{\Pi_-}=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$.
(c) [Charge, capacitance and energy of the ideal model] for any Lebesgue-measurable region $P\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ with finite positive area $A=\lambda_2(P)>0$ the charge on the portion of area $A$ of the positive plate is $Q:=\sigma A$, so $Q=(\varepsilon_0A/d)V$ with the geometric ratio
$$C:=\frac QV=\frac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}>0,$$
independent of $\sigma$ and $V$; and the field energy contained in the slab of area $A$ between the plates is
$$U=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\text{slab of area }A}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac{\sigma^2Ad}{2\varepsilon_0}=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2 .$$
(d) [Relation to the bounded-conductor theorem and scope] the linearity $Q=CV$, the positivity $C>0$ and the energy identities $U=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2$ are exactly the conclusions that [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]] proves for bounded conductor configurations with prescribed potentials and a grounded reference; this example verifies them directly for the ideal model because the infinite planes and the unbounded declared field are outside that theorem's hypotheses (compact conductors in a bounded vacuum region) and outside the declared stationary-sheet source type of [[def-em-weak-sources]], exactly as the ideal line source lies outside the compact-source types of the electrostatic page. No approximation theorem from finite plates to the infinite model is asserted; for a finite real plate pair the uniform-field model neglects the fringing field near the edges, which is not computed here, and the idealisation also omits the finite-thickness, material, transient and measurement content of any real capacitor.
items.strategy: All identities are computed directly from the explicit piecewise formulas; no compact-sheet jump theorem is invoked, because the planes are noncompact and the model is a declared idealization. (a) Local integrability is immediate from the boundedness of the piecewise field and the finiteness of the slab's intersections with compact sets ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]); the identification with regular distributions is [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]] and [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]. For a compactly supported smooth test $\psi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=-\int E\cdot\nabla\psi=+\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\int_{|x_3|<h}\partial_3\psi\,d\lambda_3$ (inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and norm of [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]); Fubini ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]) writes the slab integral as $\int_{\mathbb R^2}\bigl(\int_{-h}^{h}\partial_3\psi(x_1,x_2,s)\,ds\bigr)dx_1dx_2$, and the inner integral is $\psi(x_1,x_2,h)-\psi(x_1,x_2,-h)$ by [[thm-integration-by-parts]] (the one-dimensional Newton-Leibniz identity, applicable because $\psi$ is smooth and compactly supported and the interval is bounded); hence $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-})(\psi)$, proving the divergence identity with the sign convention of [[def-distributional-derivative]] and [[def-distribution]]. The curl identity: $E_1=E_2=0$ and $E_3=-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\mathbf 1_{\{|x_3|<h\}}$ is a function of $x_3$ alone, so its distributional $x_1$- and $x_2$-derivatives vanish identically ([[def-distributional-derivative]]); hence $\operatorname{curl}E=(\partial_2E_3-\partial_3E_2,\partial_3E_1-\partial_1E_3,\partial_1E_2-\partial_2E_1)=0$. The potential formulas give $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on the three open regions ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and continuity across the planes is the equality of the two one-sided constants. (b) is the explicit evaluation, and (c) is arithmetic with the slab integral computed by Fubini: $\int_{\text{slab}}|E|^2=\frac{\sigma^2}{\varepsilon_0^2}Ad$. (d) states the exact relation to [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]]: that theorem's structure (linearity in the voltage, positive capacitance, energy equal to half the pairing $QV$) is what the computation reproduces, but its hypotheses (bounded conductor bodies, bounded vacuum region, Dirichlet solvability) are not met by the infinite-plane idealization, so the identities are verified here directly and the theorem is not applied; the fringing qualification is the ideal-model warning recorded by the design's X2 verification, recorded as scope rather than computed. No empirical content, no measurement and no claim about real capacitors beyond the stated approximation are made. The slab in (c) is precisely $P\times(-h,h)$ for any such measurable $P$, not necessarily bounded or Jordan; the constant nonnegative integrand and finite area give the same energy by Tonelli, $\lambda_3(P\times(-h,h))=Ad$. The plane-charge portion is $\sigma\int_P1=\sigma A$. The sheet functionals are continuous on compact test supports because the projected support has finite area and the density is bounded. All test/field products and test derivatives are absolutely integrable on a common compact box. Fubini with the exact Borel product identification and finite-interval Riemann/Lebesgue comparison justifies the vertical FTC calculation and the vanishing horizontal derivatives. This example compares with the algebraic conclusions of the capacitance theorem but does not invoke its full-AC Dirichlet existence branch: its direct declared plane-model verification retains only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For merely Lebesgue-measurable $P$, choose a Borel set equal to $P$ off a Borel planar null set by [[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]]. Its product with the finite-height interval differs only inside the product of that null set with the interval, which has zero volume by the Borel product formula and Tonelli. Completeness then gives the same slab measure and integral. Thus the arbitrary measurable-area branch does not assume that every Lebesgue product set is Borel.
