items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $z,v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline, $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), let $s_0$ be an emission event with $z'(s_0)=0$ (the charge is momentarily at rest in the laboratory chart), and put $a:=z''(s_0)$ and, for $n\in S^2$, $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields of the charge given by [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and $S:=E	imes B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Then: (a) [Field on the emitted sphere] For every $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$, $$E(x_r,t_r)= rac{C\,n	imes(n	imes a)}{c^2r}+ho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|ho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C| rac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)= rac{n	imes E(x_r,t_r)}{c}.$$ (b) [Angular flux density] The limits $$ rac{dP}{d\sigma}(n):=\lim_{r	o\infty}r^2\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)= rac{C^{2}\,|n	imes(n	imes a)|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}},\qquad P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\int_{S^2} rac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)\,d\sigma(n),$$ exist with the convergence uniform in $n\in S^2$; $d\sigma$ is the polar surface measure of the unit sphere (equal to the chart surface measure by [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). (c) [Total power] $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)= rac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\cdot rac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}= rac{q^2|a|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ the Larmor power of the momentarily resting prescribed charge. (d) [Angular distribution] For $a
e0$, define $	heta\in[0,\pi]$ by $\cos	heta=(n\cdot a)/|a|$; this angle exists uniquely because the quotient is in $[-1,1]$ and cosine is continuous and strictly decreasing from $1$ to $-1$ on $[0,\pi]$. When $a=0$ the angle is undefined and $dP/d\sigma\equiv0$. Then $$ rac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)= rac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\sin^2	heta:$$ when $q
e0$ and $a
e0$ the radiation pattern vanishes exactly along the instantaneous acceleration axis and is maximal in the perpendicular plane; when $q=0$ it vanishes in every direction; $\int_{S^2}dP/d\sigma\,d\sigma=P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$. If $a=0$ all displayed radiation quantities vanish. (e) [Scope and conventions] The result is exact at an emission event at which the charge is instantaneously at rest in the laboratory chart: then $\kappa_0(n)=1$ for every $n$, so no retarded-time conversion factor appears and the displayed limits are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time. The item uses only the prescribed worldline and the retarded model fields -- it is not a mechanical evolution law, does not assert a self-force or radiation reaction, derives no mass, and makes no empirical or measurement claim. For a general emission event the exact formula and its low-speed comparison are supplied by clause (f); 'slow' motion alone is never substituted for an error bound. The prescribed curve, the uniform subluminal bound and $z'(s_0)=0$ are hypotheses; for a varying-velocity worldline the instantaneous rest event is a single parameter value, not an interval. (f) [General low-speed branch] At any emission event, without imposing $z'(s_0)=0$ for this clause, define emitted power by the weighted far-zone flux integral $\kappa_0(n)\,r^2\,n\cdot S$ on the emitted spheres, with $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot eta_0$, $ eta_0=z'(s_0)/c$, $| eta_0|\le v_*/c$ and $\gamma_0:=(1-| eta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$. The same field formula and angular computation give $$P_{\mathrm{em}}=\gamma_0^{6} igl(|a|^{2}-| eta_0	imes a|^{2} igr) rac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}.$$ Put $P_{\mathrm L}=q^{2}|a|^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$. For $| eta_0|\le\delta<1$, $$P_{\mathrm L}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L},\qquad |P_{\mathrm{em}}-P_{\mathrm L}|\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}.$$ This includes $q=0$ or $a=0$ without division by $P_{\mathrm L}$. Uniform angular comparison is also explicit: if $N_ eta=n	imes((n- eta_0)	imes a)$, $N_0=n	imes(n	imes a)$ and $H_ eta=q^{2}|N_ eta|^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{5})$, $H_0=q^{2}|N_0|^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$, then $$|H_ eta-H_0|\le rac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^3}\,\delta\left[ rac{2+\delta}{(1-\delta)^5}+ rac{5}{(1-\delta)^6}ight]$$ for all $n$. The exact rest-event clauses (a)-(e) retain their hypotheses; this additional branch supplies the general low-speed comparison, not a mechanical loss law.
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) At the emission event $s_0$ one has $\beta_0=z'(s_0)/c=0$, $\kappa_0=1$ and $\dot\beta_0=a/c$; clause (c) of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] (equivalently clause (d) of [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]], which also supplies the uniform remainder bound and the root identification $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$) gives $E_{\mathrm{vel}}=C(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)/(\kappa^3r^2)=C\,n/r^2$ and $E_{\mathrm{acc}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta)/(c\kappa^3r)=C\,n\times(n\times a)/(c^2r)$; the displayed remainder is their sum restricted to the leading term, bounded by $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$; $B=n\times E/c$. (b) For fields with $B=n\times E/c$ one has $n\cdot S=n\cdot(E\times B)/\mu_0=(|E|^2-(n\cdot E)^2)/(\mu_0c)=|n\times E|^2/(\mu_0c)$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Hence $r^2n\cdot S=r^2|n\times E|^2/(\mu_0c)$; replacing $E=E_{\mathrm{lead}}+\rho_E$ and using the bound on $\rho_E$ together with $|n\times w|\le|w|$ gives $r^2n\cdot S=C^{2}|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})+O(r^{-1})$ uniformly on $S^2$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) proves the limits and their uniformity. (c) Expand $|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}=|a|^{2}-(n\cdot a)^{2}$ and apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d): $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$, so the integral is $4\pi|a|^2-(4\pi/3)|a|^2=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$; with $C^2=q^2/(16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2)$ and $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$ the coefficient is $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})\cdot(8\pi/3)=q^2/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$. (d) The vanishing of the pattern along $\pm a$ and the value $\sin^2\theta$ follow from $n\times(n\times a)=n(n\cdot a)-a$ and $|\cdot|^2=|a|^2\cos^2\theta-2|a|^2\cos^2\theta+|a|^2=|a|^2\sin^2\theta$; the displayed coefficient is $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ by the same unit relation. The integral statement is (c). (e) At $\beta_0=0$ the emission-time Jacobian $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0$ equals $1$ for all $n$, so the retarded-time conversion factor is trivial and the fixed-sphere flux limit is the emitted power per unit emission time ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](a) for the Jacobian); the scope exclusions are those of the point-field supplier, and no mechanical, self-force or empirical conclusion is drawn. For (f), integrate the weighted angular density directly, without invoking a later item. Rotate beta=b e3 and resolve a=a_parallel e3+a_perp e1. Expanding |N_beta|² gives -(1-b²)(n dot a)²+2(1-bu)b a_parallel(n dot a)+(1-bu)²|a|², u=n3. The earlier zonal lemma supplies the azimuthal averages; the parallel coefficient reduces to1-u², perpendicular coefficient to (1-bu)²-(1-b²)(1-u²)/2. For 0<b<1, y=1-bu yields integral_-1^1 (1-u²)/(1-bu)^5 du=4/[3(1-b²)^3] and integral_-1^1 (1-bu)^-3 du=2/(1-b²)^2. An antiderivative in y for the former transformed integrand is b^-3[(1-b²)y^-4/4-2y^-3/3+y^-2/2]; the second is elementary. FTC and the chain/power rules give these identities; at b0 integrate directly, avoiding division by b. Thus integral |N_beta|²/kappa^5=(8pi/3)[gamma^6 a_parallel²+gamma^4 a_perp²], proving the general power formula. Eventwise gamma^4 P_L<=P_em<=gamma^6 P_L implies the uniform bounds since gamma>=1 and b<=delta. The difference bound follows from (1-delta²)^-3-1<=(3delta²)/(1-delta²)^3. For angular comparison |N_beta-N0|<=delta|a|, |N_beta|<= (1+delta)|a|, and the scalar mean-value bound |(1-n dot beta)^-5-1|<=5delta(1-delta)^-6 give the displayed estimate. These direct finite calculations use only the earlier point-field and zonal suppliers and the declared power/FTC rules.

items.title: Relativistic emitted power of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the setting be that of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: a charge $q\in\mathbb R$ ($C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$) on a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline $z$ in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], with retarded fields $E,B$ off the worldline and the uniform far-zone remainder of that item; let $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]). Let $s_0$ be an emission event, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\gamma_0:=(1-|\beta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$, $a:=z''(s_0)$, and for $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\kappa_0(n):=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Define the **emitted power at the emission event $s_0$** by the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}\kappa_0(n)\,r^{2}\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)\,d\sigma(n),$$ $d\sigma$ the polar surface measure (equal to the chart surface measure). The weight $\kappa_0$ is the emission-time/observation-time conversion factor of the retarded root, $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$, equivalently the moving-boundary correction $S\cdot n-(z'\cdot n)u$ at leading radiation order, where $u=|S|/c$ for the transverse far field. Then: (a) [Weighted flux limit] The limit exists and $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}\frac{\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}}{\kappa_0(n)^{5}}\,d\sigma(n).$$ (b) [Closed form and four-acceleration form] If $b:=|\beta_0|<1$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp$ is decomposed along $\beta_0=|\beta_0|e_3$ and perpendicular to it, then $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{q^{2}\gamma_0^{6}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)=\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\,\eta(A,A),$$ where $A$ is the four-acceleration of the worldline at $s_0$ and $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](e)). At $\beta_0=0$ the weight is $1$ and (b) reduces to the instantaneous-rest Larmor power of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) [Low-speed comparison] For every $\delta\in(0,1)$ and every emission event with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$, $$\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)\le\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \Bigl|P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)-\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\Bigr|\le\frac{3\delta^{2}}{(1-\delta^{2})^{3}}\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ a comparison uniform over the events with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. In particular the instantaneous-rest formula is the exact $\delta=0$ case, and no term of the comparison is asserted to be small without the explicit hypothesis $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. (d) [Scope] $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ is the power emitted at the single retarded event $s_0$ per unit emission time, defined by the weighted far-zone flux; it is not a coordinate-time loss rate of a dynamical particle, and no dynamics (self-force, radiation reaction, mass), no uniformity in $s_0$, and no empirical or measurement claim is made. The near fields are $O(r^{-2})$ with their uniform remainder as in [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]](c), so their contribution to the weighted $r^2$ flux vanishes; the $\kappa_0$-weighting is part of the definition of emitted power and is not an additional physical assumption.
items.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) On the emitted sphere the retarded data are those of the emission event ($s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]](d)), and the uniform remainder gives $E= E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}+\rho_E$ with $E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)/(c\kappa_0^{3}r)$, $|\rho_E|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ and $B=n\times E/c$. For such fields $n\cdot S=|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)$ (expand $E\times(n\times E/c)$ and use the triple-product orthogonality, [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Therefore $\kappa_0r^{2}n\cdot S=\kappa_0r^{2}|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)=\kappa_0|C|^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{6})+O(r^{-1})$ with a remainder controlled by the uniform bound ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); note $C^{2}=|C|^{2}$ as squares. Integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) gives (a) with $\dot\beta_0=a/c$ absorbed: $|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}$ replaces $c^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}$, giving $(C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5}))\int|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma$ because $|C|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}c^{2})=C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})$ and one power of $\kappa_0$ cancels. (b) Rotate the integration variable so that $\beta_0=be_3$ with $b=|\beta_0|$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp e_1$ (rotation invariance of $\sigma$, [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); put $u=n_3$ and $\kappa_0=1-bu$. Expanding the numerator with $N=n\cdot\beta_0=bu$, $d=n\cdot\dot\beta_0$ and $|n-\beta_0|^{2}=1-2bu+b^{2}$ gives, exactly as in the recorded research computation, $$\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}=-(1-b^{2})(n\cdot a)^{2}+2\kappa_0 b\,a_\parallel(n\cdot a)+\kappa_0^{2}|a|^{2}.$$ Apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](b),(c) with $f(u)=(1-bu)^{-5}$ and $g(u)=(1-bu)^{-4}$: the azimuthal average turns $(n\cdot a)^2$ into $u^{2}a_\parallel^{2}+\tfrac12(1-u^{2})a_\perp^{2}$ and $n\cdot a$ into $ua_\parallel$, and $(1-bu)^{-3}$ weights the $|a|^{2}$ term. The resulting one-dimensional integrals are elementary: $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})(1-bu)^{-5}du=\tfrac{4}{3}(1-b^{2})^{-3}$ and $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-bu)^{-3}du=2(1-b^{2})^{-2}$, both verified by the displayed antiderivatives in $y=1-bu$ using the power derivative, chain rule and fundamental theorem ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Collecting terms gives $\int|\cdot|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma=(8\pi/3)[\gamma_0^{6}a_\parallel^{2}+\gamma_0^{4}a_\perp^{2}]= (8\pi/3)\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; multiplying by $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ produces (b). The four-acceleration identity is clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], where $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_w^{6}(w\cdot a)^{2}/c^{2}$ with $w=z'(s_0)=c\beta_0$ reads $\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; the $\beta_0=0$ case is the statement of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) The strongest immediate eventwise bounds are gamma0^4 P_L<=P_em<=gamma0^6 P_L, since |a|²-|beta0 cross a|² lies between (1-b²)|a|² and |a|². With b<=delta, gamma0>=1 and gamma0^6<=(1-delta²)^-3, they imply P_L<=P_em<=(1-delta²)^-3 P_L. A larger inverse factor in the UNIFORM lower bound is not justified by an upper bound on b (the rest event b0 disproves it). The rational identity (1-delta²)^-3-1=(3delta²-3delta^4+delta^6)/(1-delta²)^3<=3delta²/(1-delta²)^3 proves the unchanged difference estimate, including P_L0. (d) records that the definition is per unit emission time, that the near-field contribution vanishes after weighting by the uniform remainder and that no dynamics or empirical content is added. To make the finite angular integration fully explicit: the parallel averaged numerator is1-u²; the perpendicular one is(1-bu)²-(1-b²)(1-u²)/2. For b>0 the first transformed antiderivative is b^-3[(1-b²)y^-4/4-2y^-3/3+y^-2/2], y=1-bu, evaluated from1-b to1+b. At b0 direct angular moments give8pi|a|²/3; never evaluate a b^-3 antiderivative at b0. The angle-axis rotation preserves the existing sphere measure.
items.physical_scope: Emitted power per unit emission time of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event on a uniformly subluminal $C^3$ worldline: the $\kappa$-weighted far-zone flux, the closed form $q^2\gamma^6(|a|^2-|\beta\times a|^2)/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^3)=q^2\eta(A,A)/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^3)$ and the uniform $\delta$-comparison with the instantaneous-rest Larmor value. Excluded: dynamical evolution, self-force, radiation reaction, mass derivation, coordinate-time loss rates, uniformity in the emission event and every empirical or measurement claim.

items.title: Self-force, runaways and finite-size regularizations are not supplied by this page
items.statement:
Every cited conditional result retains its stated hypotheses. In particular, the point-source and causal-wave comparisons below assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) through their source suppliers; this qualification supplies no additional field or self-interaction model. Record, with no speculative content, the limits of the radiation model built on this page. (a) [Self-energy] For nonzero charge $q
e0$, the truncated electrostatic field energy of the stationary idealized point charge diverges as the inner cutoff is removed ([[pthm-em-point-self-energy-divergence]]): the point source's own field carries infinite energy in this framework's idealization, and any finite-energy treatment of a point-like charge requires modifying the source or the field near the singularity, or an explicit cutoff, none of which is supplied here. The $q=0$ branch has zero field energy and no divergence. (b) [Undefined self-interaction; nonzero and zero source branches] The framework's source model [[def-em-weak-sources]] pairs distributions against compact smooth tests and expressly excludes arbitrary products of distributions. An explicit nonzero singular self-field is the stationary Coulomb field of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d): for a constant trajectory $z(t)=x_0$ and $q
e0$, $|E_q(x)|=|q|/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|^2)$ for $x
e x_0$, which tends to infinity as $x	o x_0$. Its point-source charge distribution is supported on that stationary worldline. For $q=0$, the point-source pairings of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) give $ho_{\mathrm{pt}}=J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$ for every admitted trajectory; in the stationary Coulomb source-field branch, $E_q=0$ off $x_0$ extends smoothly by zero, with $B=0$. Thus that zero-source branch has no self-field singularity and no nontrivial self-interaction. This states the source-field branch, not uniqueness among fields with an additional free field. The moving pure point-source branch retains a precise general obstruction: if $q
e0$, $z$ is an admitted $C^1$ proper trajectory, and locally integrable fields satisfy the distributional Maxwell equations with exactly its point-source pair ([[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], [[def-em-weak-sources]](b),(e)), there is no $C^1$ extension of the electric field through any interior worldline event that still satisfies those sourced equations. To see this, suppose such an extension exists near $(x_0,t_0)=(z(t_0),t_0)$ and write $g=\operatorname{div}E$. Its distributional divergence is the regular distribution of this continuous $g$ by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], under the stated Countable Choice convention. On a fixed compact box inside that neighbourhood, $|g|\le M<\infty$ by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]. Choose a spatial bump $0\le\phi_r\le1$, equal to one on $B_{r/2}(x_0)$ and supported in $B_r(x_0)$; continuity of $z$ gives a time interval $J_r$ about $t_0$, inside that fixed box's time interval, with $z(J_r)\subset B_{r/2}(x_0)$. Choose a nonzero nonnegative smooth temporal bump $\eta_r$ supported in $J_r$, with $A_r=\int\eta_r\,dt>0$ ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]]). The compact smooth test $\phi_r(x)\eta_r(t)$ has charge pairing $qA_r$, whereas its pairing with $g$ has modulus at most $M(2r)^3A_r$: the spatial support lies in the side-$2r$ cube, and iterated integration of the continuous compactly supported integrand gives this bound ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]). The sourced Gauss identity would therefore give $|q|/\varepsilon_0\le M(2r)^3$ for every sufficiently small $r>0$, an impossibility. This is a failure of a $C^1$ sourced extension, not a claim that every moving field norm blows up; the explicit norm blowup above is the stationary Coulomb case. For nonzero singular self-fields, evaluating the field on its own point-source support or forming its product with the distributional source is not supplied by these postulates. A vanishing component of the current does not remedy the singular charge-field product. More generally the prescribed moving-source framework supplies no arbitrary distribution-product operation, regularization or self-force equation; its emitted-power results below do not introduce one. No moving-source norm blowup is inferred from the stationary example, and no equation of motion is derived in either charge branch. (c) [What the emitted-power items do and do not give] [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] and [[pthm-em-lienard-emitted-power]] are prescribed-source statements: they compute the emitted power of a stipulated worldline at a stipulated emission event and determine no worldline evolution, no back-reaction and no coordinate-time rate; they are not a mechanical model. (d) [Deferred, not claimed] Extended-charge or finite-size regularizations of the self-field, the well-posedness of any self-force dynamics, runaway solutions and an electromagnetic derivation of rest mass are outside this page and are neither stated nor proved here. No experiment, measurement, statistical estimate or precision is reported or implied, and nothing in this remark is a refutation of any physical theory.

No empirical content is introduced.

items.title: A smooth pointwise subluminal curve with no retarded root at an event
items.statement: Let $c>0$ and $a>0$, and define $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ by $z(s):=(\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[thm-of-square-roots]]). Then: (a) $z$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ and $|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$; nevertheless there is no constant $v_*<c$ with $|z'(s)|\le v_*$ for all $s$, because $|z'(s)|\to c$ as $s\to\pm\infty$; (b) at the event $(x,t)=(0,0)$ the retarded equation $t-s=|x-z(s)|/c$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] has no solution in $\mathbb R$: the equation reads $-s=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$, whose right-hand side is at least $a/c>0$, and squaring both sides would give $c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}=c^{2}s^{2}$, i.e. $a^{2}=0$, contrary to $a>0$. Hence pointwise subluminality of a smooth curve does not by itself produce the retarded root, and the uniform bound $v_*<c$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]], or an explicit cone-intersection hypothesis, cannot be dropped; the supplier [[lem-em-global-retarded-root]] indeed assumes such a uniform bound. (c) [Scope] This is a mathematical example about the prescribed curve and the root equation. The curve is future timelike pointwise ($|z'(s)|<c$ for every $s$) but not uniformly subluminal; it is not asserted to be the worldline of any physical charge, and no measurement is reported. The example contradicts no theorem: it exhibits a curve lying outside the hypotheses of the root lemma.
items.strategy: Direct verification. (a) $s\mapsto c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}$ is smooth, positive and bounded below by $a^{2}>0$, and $\sqrt\cdot$ is smooth on $(0,\infty)$; the chain rule and the derivative $\tfrac{d}{dt}\sqrt t=1/(2\sqrt t)$ give $z'(s)=(c^{2}s/\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}},0,0)$, whence $|z'(s)|=c^{2}|s|/\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}<c$ for every $s$ (at $s=0$ the speed is0; for $s\ne0$ it also equals $c/\sqrt{1+a^{2}/(c^{2}s^{2})}$) ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-square-monotone]], algebra), while $|z'(s)|\to c$ as $s\to\infty$; so no $v_*<c$ bounds $|z'|$ on all of $\mathbb R$. (b) For $x=0$, $t=0$ the root equation of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] is $-s=|z(s)|/c=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$. Since the right-hand side is positive, $s<0$, so both sides of $-s=\sqrt{c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}}/c$ are positive and squaring is an equivalence: it gives $c^{2}s^{2}=c^{2}s^{2}+a^{2}$, i.e. $a^{2}=0$, contradicting $a>0$; alternatively, the root lemma's existence proof requires the uniform Lipschitz bound $|z(s_2)-z(s_1)|\le v_*|s_2-s_1|$ with $v_*<c$, which fails here. (c) states the scope; no physical or empirical interpretation is attached.
items.physical_scope: Mathematical example delimiting the kinematic hypothesis of the retarded point geometry: a smooth curve with $|z'|<c$ pointwise but no uniform bound, for which the retarded root equation fails at one event. Excluded: any claim about physical charges, any contradiction with theorems (the curve lies outside their hypotheses) and every empirical statement.

items.title: Harmonic dipole pattern and period-averaged power in the exact dipole law
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the surface and finite-source branches. Adopt the electric-dipole radiation-law idealization whose leading far fields and angular flux are the dipole expressions of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], evaluated for the prescribed smooth waveform $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ with $\omega>0$ and $p_0
e0$. This is an explicit ideal radiation-law model, not an eternal compact-time source claimed to satisfy that theorem with $D=0$. Here $r>0$, $u\in\mathbb R$, $p_0\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ carries C m, $\omega$ carries s$^{-1}$, and $e_1,e_2,e_3$ are the standard orthonormal spatial basis. The waveform is an explicitly prescribed time-dependent dipole moment as defined in [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], not measured data; [[def-em-electric-moments]] supplies only the static moment convention. All exact quantities below refer to that ideal leading radiation law. Then: (a) [Fields] With $n=\sin	heta\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin	heta\sin\varphi\,e_2+\cos	heta\,e_3$, $	heta\in[0,\pi]$, $\varphi\in[0,2\pi]$, the ideal leading far fields are $$E_{\mathrm{lead}}(rn,u+r/c)=- rac{\mu_0\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)}{4\pi r}\,n	imes(n	imes e_3),\qquad B_{\mathrm{lead}}= rac{n	imes E_{\mathrm{lead}}}{c},$$ with $|n	imes(n	imes e_3)|=|\sin	heta|$, so the amplitude pattern is $\propto\sin	heta$ and vanishes on the dipole axis $	heta\in\{0,\pi\}$. (b) [Angular power density] The retarded-time angular power density of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] is $$ rac{dP}{d\sigma}(n,u)= rac{\mu_0|n	imes p''(u)|^{2}}{16\pi^{2}c}= rac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{16\pi^{2}c}\,\sin^{2}	heta,$$ the $\sin^{2}	heta$ pattern with zeros along $\pm e_3$ and maximum in the equatorial plane when $\cos(\omega u)
e0$; at times with $\cos(\omega u)=0$ the density vanishes in every direction; its integral over the sphere is $$\int_{S^2} rac{dP}{d\sigma}d\sigma= rac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c},$$ using $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}	heta\,d\sigma=8\pi/3$ from [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](a). (c) [Period average] The mean of the total power over one retarded-time period $u\in[0,2\pi/\omega]$ is $$ rac{\omega}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi/\omega} rac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)}{6\pi c}\,du= rac{\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}}{12\pi c}.$$ (d) [Scope] The computation is the exact dipole law of the model; a finite prescribed source realizes it only within the absolute error bound of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] with its $D(u)$, and a physical antenna's feed, current distribution and material realization are additional source models not supplied here. The average in (c) is taken in the retarded-time variable, not in observation time; no measurement, radiation resistance, matching condition or effective area is reported, and no empirical claim is made. (e) [Actual compact-window realization] Choose a compact smooth time cutoff $\eta\equiv1$ near one selected period, a nonnegative $C^\infty$ bump $\sigma$ supported in $B_a$ with integral $1$, and $p_\eta(u)=\eta(u)p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$. Define $ho(y,u)=-p_\eta(u)\cdot
abla\sigma(y)$, $J(y,u)=p_\eta'(u)\sigma(y)$. These are smooth compact spacetime sources, satisfy continuity, carry zero total charge and have moment $p_\eta$. On the chosen period the moment equals the harmonic waveform, while the actual retarded field has the full $D(u)$, $\Gamma_E/r^{2}$ and $(\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c)/r^{2}$ errors of the dipole theorem. Its asymptotic total-power deviation from the ideal law is bounded by that theorem's explicit $R(u)$; its period-averaged deviation is bounded by the average of $|R(u)|$. The condition $V=p''$ is a sufficient ideal transverse-moment condition; it is not equivalent to $D=0$. No eternal nonzero harmonic moment is asserted for a compact-time source.
items.strategy: Direct substitution in [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. (a) $p(u)=p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ gives $p''(u)=-\omega^{2}p_0\cos(\omega u)e_3$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives|the scalar multiple rule]]), and clause (c) of the theorem gives $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times p'')/(4\pi r)$ with $B_{\mathrm{lead}}=n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}/c$ up to the stated errors; these are the ideal leading amplitudes; a finite-radius compact-source field still has its Gamma/r² remainder, even if a dipole-replacement error happens to vanish. The identity $n\times(n\times e_3)=n(n\cdot e_3)-e_3$ with $n\cdot e_3=\cos\theta$ and the Pythagorean identity give $|n\times(n\times e_3)|=|\sin\theta|$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]). (b) Clause (d) of the theorem gives the limit $\mu_0/(16\pi^{2}c)\int|n\times V|^{2}d\sigma$ with $V=p''$; substituting $p''$ and using $|n\times p''|^{2}=|p''|^{2}\sin^{2}\theta$ yields the displayed density. Its integral uses $\int_{S^2}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})du=2\pi\cdot(4/3)=8\pi/3$ by [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](a) with $f(u)=1-u^{2}$; multiplying $\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)/(16\pi^{2}c)$ by $8\pi/3$ gives $\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}\cos^{2}(\omega u)/(6\pi c)$. (c) The average uses $\int_0^{2\pi/\omega}\cos^{2}(\omega u)du=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$: substitute $v=\omega u$ or exhibit the antiderivative $\tfrac{u}{2}+\tfrac{\sin(2\omega u)}{4\omega}$ and evaluate at the endpoints by the fundamental theorem ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]); multiplying the mean value of $\cos^{2}$ by the coefficient gives the displayed result. (d) states the scope; no measured or fitted quantity appears, and the period average is explicitly in retarded time. For (e), choose a nonnegative smooth compact cutoff positive on a ball, normalize by its strictly positive finite Lebesgue integral, and scale that unit-mass bump to have support inside B_a ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]]) and eta by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Continuity is rho_t=-p_eta' dot grad sigma and div J=p_eta' dot grad sigma. Integration by parts with zero boundary gives integral rho0 and integral y_i rho=p_eta_i integral sigma=p_eta_i. Therefore [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] constructs the actual fields; [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] gives their moment identities and complete finite-radius and flux errors, not an exact D0 premise for a time-varying harmonic current. Integrating the absolute error over one selected period gives the claimed average-error bound.
items.physical_scope: Deterministic model computation in the exact electric-dipole law for declared parameters: the $\sin^2\theta$ angular pattern and period-averaged power $\mu_0\omega^{4}p_0^{2}/(12\pi c)$ of a prescribed harmonic dipole moment, together with an actual compact-window source realization carrying the dipole theorem's explicit finite-radius and flux errors. Excluded: antenna feed, material and matching models, radiation resistance, measurements and every empirical statement.

items.title: Conditional radius loss of a prescribed slowly orbiting charge in a reduced quasistatic model
items.statement: When invoking the cited point-source emitted-power theorem as an established interpretation, retain its Countable Choice premise ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]). The reduced loss-rate formula in (H) below is independently adopted as a modelling hypothesis; the conditional finite-calculus orbit computation from (H) uses no choice. Adopt the following idealized, hypothetical setup of a prescribed slowly orbiting charge; it is a thought experiment with explicit premises, not a reported measurement. (H) Let $m>0$ be an externally supplied rest mass and $q\ne0$ a charge parameter ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]), let $\kappa>0$ carry J m, and let $J_t\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, $t_0\in J_t$, and $r:J_t\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$, with $r_0:=r(t_0)>0$. The reduced model assigns to each radius the circular-orbit values about a fixed laboratory centre ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]) for the attractive potential $V(r)=-\kappa/r$: the circular-orbit energy is $E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r)=-\kappa/(2r)$ and the circular orbit with speed $v$ satisfies $mv^{2}=\kappa/r$, with centripetal acceleration $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$. These are instantaneous circular reference values, not the exact kinematics of a curve with varying radius. To specify the intended validity window, choose dimensionless bounds $0<\delta_v,\delta_a<1$ and require $v(t)/c\le\delta_v$ and $T_{\rm orb}(t)|r'(t)|/r(t)\le\delta_a$, where $v(t):=\sqrt{\kappa/(mr(t))}$ and $T_{\rm orb}(t):=2\pi r(t)/v(t)$; the second ratio measures fractional radius change in one reference period. Independently adopt that the electromagnetic energy emitted per unit time is instantaneously taken to be the Larmor value $q^{2}a(t)^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] evaluated at the instantaneous centripetal acceleration, so that the adopted energy balance of the reduced model reads $$\frac{d}{dt}E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r(t))=-\frac{q^{2}a(t)^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}.$$ Then, with $A:=q^{2}\kappa/(3\pi\varepsilon_0m^{2}c^{3})>0$: (a) the reduced model implies $r'(t)=-A/r(t)^{2}$ for all $t$ where the model applies, and the circular orbit radius in the reduced model obeys $$r(t)^{3}=r_{0}^{3}-3A(t-t_{0})$$ on any interval containing $t_0$ on which $r>0$; (b) $r$ is strictly decreasing on $J_t$. The scalar balance ODE, considered without the validity-window inequalities, has the unique maximal positive continuation $\widehat r(t):=(r_0^3-3A(t-t_0))^{1/3}$ on $(-\infty,t_*)$, where $t_*:=t_0+r_0^3/(3A)$. It restricts to $r$ on $J_t$ and satisfies $\widehat r(t)\downarrow0$ as $t\uparrow t_*$; assigning zero at $t_*$ is only a continuous endpoint extension, not a positive-radius solution; (c) [Scope and qualifications] the deduction is conditional on (H). The low-speed premise $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\ll c^{2}$ necessarily fails as $r\to0$, so the model's own hypotheses break down near the collapse time and the computation is not a proof that a physical orbit reaches $r=0$; it is not a derivation of atomic lifetimes, not a coupled point-particle self-force calculation (that dynamics is not available in this framework), and it supplies no empirical evidence. The reduced-model finite-time collapse is retained as a mathematical property of (H), while all conclusions about nature remain conditional on (H) and on its regime of validity. No measurement, dataset, statistical model or uncertainty is introduced.
items.strategy: A complete conditional deduction from (H). (a) Differentiate $E_{\mathrm{orb}}(r)=-\kappa/(2r)$ along $r(t)$: the power rule gives $\tfrac{d}{dt}(-\kappa/(2r))=\kappa r'/(2r^{2})$ ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); the balance (H) reads $\kappa r'/(2r^{2})=-q^{2}a^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$; substituting $a=\kappa/(mr^{2})$ and solving for $r'$ gives $r'=-q^{2}\kappa/(3\pi\varepsilon_0m^{2}c^{3}r^{2})=-A/r^{2}$. Multiplying by $3r^{2}$ gives $\tfrac{d}{dt}(r^{3})=-3A$, and the fundamental theorem applied on any interval where $r>0$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[def-interval]]) yields the displayed cubic; equivalently, differentiating the cubic reproduces the ODE, so the two are equivalent in the reduced model. (b) $r'=-A/r^{2}<0$ since $A>0$, so $r$ is strictly decreasing wherever the model applies; from the cubic, $r(t)^{3}\downarrow0$ as $t\uparrow t_{*}=t_{0}+r_{0}^{3}/(3A)$, and $r(t)^{3}<0$ beyond $t_{*}$ records the breakdown rather than a negative radius. (c) The scope clause records the failure of $v^{2}=\kappa/(mr)\ll c^{2}$ as $r\to0$, the absence of any coupled self-force dynamics in the framework (the point self-field is singular and its product with the current is undefined, as recorded by the scope remark on this page), and the absence of empirical content: this is a mapped, reduced model with a finite-time formal collapse, exactly as stated, and the conclusion is conditional on (H) throughout. The Larmor energy-loss expression is explicitly ADOPTED in(H) for the reduced slowly orbiting mechanical model, not obtained by pretending each laboratory orbit event is a rest event. The preceding Larmor theorem supplies the rest law and quantified general low-speed comparison; converting a prescribed emitted power into this mechanical balance remains the separate assumption(H). The ODE deduction itself uses only the stated scalar balance and finite calculus, and proves no self-force law.
items.physical_scope: Reduced quasistatic circular-orbit model with an adopted Larmor energy-balance premise (H): the radius ODE $r'=-A/r^{2}$, the cubic solution $r^{3}=r_{0}^{3}-3A(t-t_{0})$ and the formal finite-time collapse limit as a property of (H). Excluded: any claim that a physical orbit reaches the centre or an atom decays in finite time; coupled self-force dynamics; derivation of lifetimes; measurements, statistical models and every empirical claim.

pages.title: Lorentz covariant formulation

items.title: Tensor Maxwell equations equal the four laboratory Maxwell equations
items.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I	imes\Omega$ with its inertial chart $x$, the electric and magnetic fields $E,B$ of [[def-em-fields]], the source fields $(ho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]] with $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be those of the framework, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with the components fixed there, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let $j=(cho,J)$ carry the tensor-component identification adopted in [[def-em-sources]]. Assume the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]: $E,B$ are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega	imes I$ with the additional derivatives required by each displayed equation existing and continuous, and $ho,J$ are continuous. Write $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ and $\partial_i$ for the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and $\operatorname{div},\operatorname{curl}$ for those of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then: (a) [Equivalence] On $I	imes\Omega$ the four smooth-branch equations $$\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$ hold if and only if the two systems $$(\mathrm{TM1})\quad \partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0\,j^
u\ (
u=0,1,2,3),\qquad (\mathrm{TM2})\quad \partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\mu}=0\ (\lambda,\mu,
u\in\{0,1,2,3\})$$ hold on $I	imes\Omega$. Every instance of $(\mathrm{TM2})$ with a repeated index vanishes identically because $F$ is alternating, so $(\mathrm{TM1})$ and $(\mathrm{TM2})$ carry exactly eight independent scalar equations: $(\mathrm{TM1})$ with $
u=0$ is $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$ (using $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$), $(\mathrm{TM1})$ with $
u=i$ is the $i$-th component of $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, $(\mathrm{TM2})$ with $(\lambda,\mu,
u)=(1,2,3)$ is $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and the three cyclic triples $(0,i,j)$ are the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$; conversely these eight scalar equations reproduce the two systems. (b) [Form invariance under a change of inertial description] Let $x'$ be another inertial chart with transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$, $\Lambda$ a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix (the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]), and let the primed components of the same objects be the tensor components of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii): $F'^{\,ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$, $F'_{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(\Lambda^{-1})^d{}_bF_{cd}$, $j'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bj^b$. Then $(\mathrm{TM1})$ holds in $x$ if and only if $(\mathrm{TM1})$ holds in $x'$ with $j'$, and $(\mathrm{TM2})$ holds in $x$ if and only if it holds in $x'$; by (a) applied in both charts the four smooth-branch equations are likewise form-invariant, the primed fields satisfying the primed equations with the primed sources. (c) [Hypotheses actually used] Only first derivatives of $E,B$ occur; the equivalence uses exactly the component dictionary, the alternating character of $F$, the constants $\mu_0,c,\varepsilon_0$ and the identification $j=(cho,J)$, and the covariance clause uses the constant-coefficient component law and the invertibility of $\Lambda$. No potential, no second derivative, no boundary, decay or smoothness hypothesis beyond the stated class, and no converse from the wave equations to the Maxwell equations is used or asserted. (d) [Scope] Only the smooth branch is covered; the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and field or source points of singular support are excluded. The conventions $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ fix the signs of $(\mathrm{TM1})$, and the alternative sign convention, which reverses the form of the sourced equation, is not mixed with them. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates, uses no choice principle and makes no empirical claim.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation, then the transformation law. (a) Substitute the displayed components: $\partial_\mu F^{\mu0}=\partial_iF^{i0}=-\operatorname{div}E/c$ versus $-\mu_0j^0=-\mu_0c\rho$ gives $\operatorname{div}E=\mu_0c^2\rho=\rho/\varepsilon_0$; $\partial_\mu F^{\mu i}=\partial_0F^{0i}+\partial_jF^{ji}=c^{-2}\partial_tE_i-(\operatorname{curl}B)_i$ versus $-\mu_0j^i$ gives the $i$-th Ampère component; $\partial_1F_{23}+\partial_2F_{31}+\partial_3F_{12}=\operatorname{div}B$; and the cyclic sums $\partial_0F_{ij}+\partial_iF_{j0}+\partial_jF_{0i}=c^{-1}\left(\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_tB_k+\partial_iE_j-\partial_jE_i\right)$ for the three cyclic pairs $(i,j)$ give the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. Each display is an identity after substituting the components, so both implications follow; no derivative is commuted and no epsilon-identity beyond the coordinate definition of the components is used. (b) For $(\mathrm{TM1})$: $\partial'_aF'^{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\Lambda^a{}_e\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{ef}=\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{cf}$ by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iv) and orthogonality $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$, so $\partial_cF^{cf}=-\mu_0j^f$ is equivalent to $\partial'_aF'^{ab}=-\mu_0j'^b$. For $(\mathrm{TM2})$ the three derivative factors contribute the same trilinear factor $(\Lambda^{-1})^{\otimes3}$ to the cyclic sum, and $\Lambda^{-1}$ is invertible; hence zero is preserved in both directions. No physical equivalence of descriptions is proved: clause (b) is conditional on the adoption of [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]].
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about the smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell postulate on the laboratory region: the four SI Maxwell equations are equivalent to the two tensor equations for the components of the electromagnetic two-form and four-current fixed by [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and [[def-em-sources]], with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $x^0=ct$, $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$, and form-invariance under proper orthochronous changes of inertial chart. Excluded: the weak branch, singular source support, magnetic charge, potentials, and any dynamics beyond the adopted equations; no empirical claim.

items.title: Covariance, boosts and the two field invariants
items.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart $x$ of the framework ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]), $k\ge1$, with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $\Lambda_\beta$ be the explicit boost of [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] with $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero. Let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the corresponding inertial chart, and for every event $p$ in the overlap of the two chart restrictions define the primed field components by reading the components of the same $F$ in $x'$ through the dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], so that $F'_{0i}=-E'_i/c$, $F'_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$ at $p$. Then: (a) [Boosted fields] at every such $p$, with $\parallel$ and $\perp$ the components along and orthogonal to $e_1$ in the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart, $$E'_1=E_1,\quad B'_1=B_1,\qquad E'_\parallel=E_\parallel,\quad B'_\parallel=B_\parallel,\qquad E'_\perp=\gamma\,(E+v\times B)_\perp,\qquad B'_\perp=\gamma\,(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp,$$ equivalently, componentwise, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-\beta cB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+\beta cB_2)$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$. (a′) [Arbitrary boost direction] For a velocity vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|v|<c$, use the actual vector boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]], with $\gamma_v=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. If $v\ne0$, decompose the fields along $\widehat v=v/|v|$ and its orthogonal complement. Then $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$. Equivalently, for every $v$, including $v=0$, $$E'=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot E)}{c^2},\qquad B'=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot B)}{c^2}.$$ At $v=0$ these are the identity and no preferred parallel direction is assigned.  (b) [Invariants] at every such $p$, $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B;$$ equivalently the scalar fields $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) take the same values whether computed from the components in $x$ or in $x'$. (c) [General proper orthochronous changes] for any proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix $\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$, the primed components of $F$ are given by the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii), $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$; in particular, if $\Lambda=\widehat R$ is the extension of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), then $E'=RE$ and $B'=RB$, and by the unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii) every proper orthochronous change acts first by $(E,B)\mapsto(RE,RB)$ and then by the arbitrary-direction boost law (a′) with velocity $-c\beta$, where $\beta$ is the vector parameter of that factorization. The axis-only law (a) is not substituted for a general vector boost. (d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and $(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then $(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]. (e) [Scope] All clauses are pointwise on the overlap $U\cap U'$ of the two chart restrictions, are conditional on the adopted postulates, and concern the smooth classical flat branch; no accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, material medium, apparatus or empirical claim is involved; the transformation is exact algebra, and the primed component functions are $C^k$ wherever the overlap is open. The invariants clause uses only the proper orthochronous changes of description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's field conventions ([[def-em-fields]]).
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation from the transformation law, then the scalar contractions. (a) Apply $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii); $\Lambda_\beta$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map by [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]]) to the raised components: $F'^{01}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^1{}_1F^{01}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^1{}_0F^{10}=\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)F^{01}=F^{01}$, $F'^{02}=\gamma(E_2/c-\beta B_3)$, $F'^{03}=\gamma(E_3/c+\beta B_2)$, $F'^{12}=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, $F'^{13}=\gamma(-B_2-\beta E_3/c)$, $F'^{23}=F^{23}$. Reading $E'_i=cF'^{0i}$ and $B'_k$ from the appropriate cyclic entries through the dictionary gives the displayed components; the vector form evaluates $v\times B$ and $v\times E$ from [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (a′) For $v\ne0$ put $u=v/|v|$. Choose a coordinate vector $e_j$ not parallel to $u$, set $a=(e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u)/|e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u|$ and $b=u\times a$. Direct cross-product coordinates show $(u,a,b)$ is an oriented orthonormal basis. Let $R$ have these vectors as rows, so $Ru=e_1$, $R^{\mathsf T}R=I$ and $\det R=1$; only one finite choice is used. Substituting the matrix of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $B(v/c)=\widehat R^{-1}\Lambda_{|v|/c}\widehat R$. Apply the rotation component law proved in (c), then the axis computation (a), then rotate back. The determinant-one cofactor identity gives $R(p\times q)=(Rp)\times(Rq)$, yielding the parallel/perpendicular formulas. Use $\gamma_v-1=\gamma_v^2|v|^2/(c^2(\gamma_v+1))$ to combine the pieces into the displayed nonsingular vector formulas; at zero the separately defined boost is the identity.  (b) The two expressions are the two independent scalar contractions of the two-form; substituting the component law into $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ with $\eta'=\eta$ shows invariance, equivalently clauses (c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) identifies them with $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $4E\cdot B/c$. (c) For the rotation case $\Lambda^0{}_0=1$, $\Lambda^0{}_j=\Lambda^i{}_0=0$, $\Lambda^i{}_j=R^i{}_j$ give $F'^{0i}=R^i{}_jF^{0j}$ and $F'^{ij}=R^i{}_kR^j{}_lF^{kl}$; reading the dictionary and using $\det R=1$ in the cofactor identity $\epsilon_{nij}R^i{}_kR^j{}_lR^n{}_m=\epsilon_{klm}$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-linear-operator]], [[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]) gives $E'=RE$, $B'=RB$. The general case is the actual unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii). Since components transform by multiplication with $\Lambda$, first apply $\widehat R$ and then $B(-\beta)$; the latter uses (a′) with vector velocity $-c\beta$, not the nonnegative axis parameter of (a). (d) Chain clauses (a)-(c) with [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]: clause (a) of that theorem in both charts plus its clause (b) for the pair of descriptions. No potential, no second derivative of the fields, no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement on the smooth branch of the framework's Maxwell fields in one inertial chart: the exact passive-boost component formulas for $E,B$ along one spatial axis and in every vector direction (including the zero boost), invariance of $B^2-E^2/c^2$ and $E\cdot B$ under every proper orthochronous change of inertial description, the rotation and general-factorization laws, and form-invariance of the four Maxwell equations. Excluded: accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, media, weak or singular fields, orientation-reversing changes, apparatus and any measurement or empirical claim.

items.title: Observer field split and exact classical wave Doppler reading
items.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] in SI units ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), $k\ge1$, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $n\in V$ be a future unit observer vector, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$ and positive rest metric ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)), and suppose its coordinate velocity in the laboratory frame is $w$, $|w|<c$, so that $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ with $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e)). Then: (a) [Observer split and measured vectors] with $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ as in [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$, $e^\sharp,b^\sharp\in n^\perp$, the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ (so the six rest components $(e,b)$ determine $F$ at the event), and in the laboratory frame $$e_i=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\bigl(E_i+(w\times B)_i\bigr),\qquad b_i=-\gamma_w\Bigl(B_i-\frac{(w\times E)_i}{c^2}\Bigr),\qquad e_0=-\frac{\gamma_w}{c^2}E\cdot w,\qquad b_0=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}B\cdot w.$$ Define the measured electric and magnetic vectors $E_n:=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n:=-b^\sharp$, the covectors first restricted to $n^\perp$ and raised with its positive rest metric (equivalently their spacetime metric-dual vectors, since both annihilate $n$); under the model assumption (A1) that an ideal field detector comoving with the observer at the reception event reads the components of $F$ in the observer's rest frame — equivalently that $E_n$ and $B_n$ are the electric and magnetic fields read there — the observed components are, in the observer's inertial rest frame, the arbitrary-direction boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′) for the vector parameter $\beta=w/c$: the components along $w$ equal $E_\parallel$ and $B_\parallel$, and the components perpendicular to $w$ equal $\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$. At $w=0$ the observer is the laboratory rest observer and reads $E,B$ themselves; there is no distinguished direction of motion. Orthogonality means $e(n)=b(n)=0$, not vanishing temporal covector components in an unrelated laboratory frame. (b) [Plane wave and exact frequency reading] let $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$ be the data of a plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] whose amplitude equations hold as in [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so that the pair is a source-free smooth Maxwell field and $s$ is the propagation direction. Then the phase covector with components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ in the laboratory frame is a nonzero future null covector, and under the ideal-plane-wave reading rule of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (ii) the observer reads the exact angular frequency $$\omega_n:=-c\,k(n)=\gamma_w\Bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\Bigr)\omega>0,$$ with the direction transformation (aberration), longitudinal formulas and two transverse protocols of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(v) apply with their nonzero-motion qualifications; at $w=0$ frequency and direction are unchanged. Successive inertial changes act on the same phase covector by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii); each stage updates the direction as well as the frequency, and positive successive frequency ratios multiply. This composition statement is a direct covector/reading calculation, not a nonexistent composition clause of the Doppler supplier. (c) [Status and scope] the observer split, the nullity of $k$ and the frequency formula are conditional deductions from the stated items, while the identification of $(E_n,B_n)$ and of $\omega_n$ with apparatus readings is the explicitly adopted ideal-detector model assumption (A1) together with the ideal-plane-wave model [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for the clock and light readings); no calibration, apparatus, statistical or empirical claim is made, no photon model and no identification of frequency with energy by a factor $\hbar$ is used, and the statement is pointwise at a reception event: the decomposition and the reconstruction of clause (a) hold pointwise for any future unit observer $n$, while the frequency and aberration readings of clause (b) are stated for inertial observers — an accelerating observer requires its own analysis, since differentiating the decomposition adds derivatives of $n$ — and media, dispersion, modulation, boundaries and finite line widths are outside the item.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** evaluate the observer decomposition of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] at the given $n$, then apply the exact SR Doppler theorem to the wave data. (a) Directly evaluate the adopted dictionary at $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$: $e_0=-\gamma_w E\cdot w/c^2$, $e_i=\gamma_w(E_i+(w\times B)_i)/c$. The dual dictionary is $(*F)_{0i}=B_i$, $(*F)_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}E_k/c$, so $b_0=\gamma_w B\cdot w/c$ and $b_i=-\gamma_w(B_i-(w\times E)_i/c^2)$. In particular $n^ae_a=n^ab_a=0$, using $w\cdot(w\times B)=w\cdot(w\times E)=0$; antisymmetry gives the same annihilation intrinsically. Raising with the spacetime metric maps these annihilating covectors into $n^\perp$, and its restriction agrees with the positive rest-space musical isomorphism. The reconstruction is exactly [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] (a). The vector boost [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $w/c$ sends $n$ to $(1,0,0,0)$: its temporal component is $\gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2)=1$ and the spatial block cancels. Thus its primed oriented axes are the observer's canonical inertial rest axes. Apply the repaired arbitrary-direction law [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′); in those axes $e'_0=b'_0=0$, $E'_i=c e'_i$ and $B'_i=-b'_i$, giving exactly the measured-vector components under assumption (A1). For $w=0$ the boost is the identity. No rest-space metric lowering can erase a nonzero laboratory component; the two component descriptions are distinct. (b) The amplitude equations give $|k|=\omega/c$ and $s=k/|k|$ with $|s|=1$ ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (b)); raising with $\eta$ gives $k^0=\omega/c>0$, $k^i=(\omega/c)s^i$ and $\eta(k^\sharp,k^\sharp)=-(\omega/c)^2+(\omega/c)^2|s|^2=0$, so $k$ is future null and nonzero. The data $(\omega,s)$ therefore satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]], whose clauses (i)-(v) give $\omega_n=\gamma_w(1-w\cdot s/c)\omega>0$, the aberrated direction and the longitudinal/transverse cases; the reading rule is clause (ii) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]. For successive changes $x_1=\Lambda_1x_0+b_1$, $x_2=\Lambda_2x_1+b_2$, the covector laws give $k_2=(\Lambda_2^{-1})^{\mathsf T}(\Lambda_1^{-1})^{\mathsf T}k_0=((\Lambda_2\Lambda_1)^{-1})^{\mathsf T}k_0$. The affine phase constant transforms with the translations as in [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii). Apply the positive frequency reading at each stage, obtaining $\omega_2/\omega_0=(\omega_2/\omega_1)(\omega_1/\omega_0)$ with the correctly updated intermediate direction. (c) records the adopted interpretation premise (A1) and the scope; no choice principle is used and no empirical premise enters.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about the smooth framework fields at one event: the decomposition of the field into the rest components of a future unit observer, the reconstruction of $F$, the measured electric and magnetic vectors of an inertial observer with coordinate velocity $w$, and the exact angular-frequency reading and aberration of an ideal plane wave, with the ideal-detector and ideal-plane-wave model assumptions stated. Excluded: apparatus calibration, real detectors, accelerated observers, media and dispersion, modulation, finite line widths, intensity and polarization measurement, quantum photon models, and any statistical or empirical claim.

items.title: The four-force equation reproduces the coordinate Lorentz force and power
items.statement: Assume the framework's spacetime, field and worldline objects of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and clause (i) of the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]: a constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-sources]] (a), an externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline $x:J\to A$ with four-velocity $U$, and a prescribed field $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle; the adopted equation of motion is $$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),\qquad \eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u),$$ $U$ the four-velocity of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b) with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $t\mapsto r(t)$ be the laboratory chart reading of the worldline, $v:=r'$ its coordinate velocity and $\gamma:=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so that $U=\gamma(c,v)$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)). Then, wherever the worldline is $C^2$: (a) [Coordinate force and power] with the coordinate three-momentum $p:=m\gamma v$ of [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a), $$\frac{dp}{dt}=q\,(E+v\times B),\qquad \frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=q\,E\cdot v,$$ the derivatives taken with respect to the chart time $t$ and $E,B$ the components of $F$ in the laboratory frame. (b) [Norm preservation] $s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant on $J$ with value $-c^2$; in particular a solution with future timelike initial data remains future timelike, and $|v(t)|<c$ wherever the reading is differentiable ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]). (c) [Controlled low-speed expansion] for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, on any interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$, $$|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\Bigl(\frac{|v|^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{2},$$ and consequently $$|p-mv|\le m|v|\,\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma mc^2-mc^2-\tfrac12m|v|^2\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\frac{m|v|^4}{c^2};$$ the constants depend only on $\delta$, so the bounds are uniform in $|v|/c\le\delta$. These are pointwise algebraic expansions; they assert no approximation of the trajectory over a time interval, which would require a separate stability argument. (d) [Scope] The charge is constant, $m>0$ is an externally supplied parameter and $F$ is a prescribed exterior field: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles and zero or variable mass; the nonrelativistic coordinate law is not adopted as exact, and (c) is a controlled kinematic expansion, not a trajectory approximation. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** contract the field with the four-velocity in the fixed component dictionary, then apply the mean value theorem to $(1-z)^{-1/2}$. (a) With $\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]) and $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $U_\nu=\gamma(-c,v)$: $q\,\Phi(U)^i=q\gamma\bigl(cF^i{}_0+F^i{}_jv^j\bigr)=q\gamma(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ since $F^i{}_0=\eta_{00}F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^i{}_j=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; and $q\,\Phi(U)^0=q\gamma E\cdot v/c$. Since $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q\Phi(U)^i$ and $d/dt=\gamma^{-1}d/d\tau$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)), $dp_i/dt=\gamma^{-1}\,q\gamma(E+v\times B)_i=q(E+v\times B)_i$ with $p=m\gamma v$ from [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a); the temporal component gives $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=qE\cdot v$ after multiplying by $c$. (b) $\eta(U,U)$ has derivative $2\eta(U,U')=2(q/m)\eta(U,\Phi(U))=0$ by the orthogonality clause of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] (which needs no derivative of the field); the initial value $-c^2$ is that of the four-velocity. For the stated solution-preservation conclusion, differentiability makes $U$ continuous and the norm identity gives $(U^0)^2=c^2+|U_{\mathrm{sp}}|^2\ge c^2$. Thus $U^0$ cannot vanish; on a connected interval its sign cannot change by [[thm-intermediate-value]]. Positive initial $U^0$ therefore stays positive and the solution stays in the future timelike component. This conditional argument asserts no existence or continuation of solutions. (c) $z:=|v|^2/c^2$ and $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}$; by [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]], $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$ and $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$ with $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. At $z=0$ all stated differences and bounds are zero directly; henceforth assume $0<z\le\delta^2$. First-order bound by the mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]): $|f(z)-1|=|f'(\xi)|z\le z\,/\,(2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2})$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, using monotonicity of the positive power ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]]). Second-order remainder by Cauchy's mean value theorem ([[thm-cauchy-mean-value]]) applied on $[0,z]$ to $q(s):=f(s)-1-\tfrac s2$ and $g(s):=s^2$: $q(z)/z^2=q'(\xi)/g'(\xi)=(f'(\xi)-\tfrac12)/(2\xi)$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, and the mean value theorem on $[0,\xi]$ applied to $f'$ gives $f'(\xi)-\tfrac12=f'(\xi)-f'(0)=\xi f''(\eta)$ for some $\eta\in(0,\xi)$, so $|f(z)-1-\tfrac z2|=\tfrac12|f''(\eta)|z^2\le\tfrac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}z^2$. The two displays for $p$ and $\gamma mc^2$ are the multiplication of these bounds by $m|v|$ and $mc^2$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] for the product $p=m\gamma v$). (d) The scope clause records the postulates and exclusions; no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about one charged massive particle of constant charge and positive external rest mass moving on a future timelike $C^2$ worldline in a prescribed exterior electromagnetic field that is $C^1$ near the graph, under the adopted covariant coupling: the coordinate Lorentz force and power, preservation of the four-velocity norm, and uniform low-speed bounds with constants depending only on the speed interval. Excluded: the particle's own field, radiation reaction, self-force, magnetic monopoles, variable or zero mass, trajectory approximation over time without a stability argument, and any measurement or empirical claim.

items.title: The covariant field stress-energy tensor and its balance law
items.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I	imes\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]: $E,B$ jointly $C^1$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] with the additional derivatives required by each Maxwell equation existing and continuous, continuous sources $(ho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components, $j=(cho,J)$ the four-current, $u$ and $S$ the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and $g$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$ the momentum density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Define the stress-energy tensor of the field by $$T^{\mu
u}:= rac{1}{\mu_0}\Bigl(F^{\mu\alpha}F^
u{}_\alpha- rac14\eta^{\mu
u}F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta}\Bigr).$$ Then: (a) [Object] $T$ is a symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] with $\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}$ continuous on $U$, it is traceless, $\eta_{\mu
u}T^{\mu
u}=0$, and under a proper orthochronous change of inertial chart with transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$ its components transform as $T'^{\mu
u}=\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^
u{}_ eta T^{\alpha eta}$ ([[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)). (b) [Components] in the laboratory frame $$T^{00}=u= rac{\varepsilon_0|E|^2}{2}+ rac{|B|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{0i}=T^{i0}= rac{S_i}{c}=c\,g_i= rac{(E	imes B)_i}{\mu_0c},\qquad T^{ij}=-\sigma_{ij},$$ where $\sigma_{ij}=\varepsilon_0 igl(E_iE_j-	frac12\delta_{ij}|E|^2 igr)+\mu_0^{-1} igl(B_iB_j-	frac12\delta_{ij}|B|^2 igr)$; in particular the spatial block is minus the Maxwell stress of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. (c) [Balance] under the smooth branch, $$\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}=-f^
u,\qquad f^
u:=F^{
u\lambda}j_\lambda,$$ where algebraically $f=(J\cdot E/c,ho E+J	imes B)$. Its interpretation as the electromagnetic four-force density delivered to matter uses the separately adopted continuum coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (ii) for matter models and sources satisfying that postulate's hypotheses. The component identities are $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$ and $\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-(ho E+J	imes B)$ of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a) and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (a). (d) [Matter coupling and finite-flux conservation] let $T_{\mathrm m}$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field on $U$ satisfying $\partial_\mu T_{\mathrm m}{}^{\mu
u}=f^
u$ (an adopted matter model, not derived here); then $\partial_\mu(T+T_{\mathrm m})^{\mu
u}=0$, on every finite axis-parallel box with an open neighbourhood contained in $U$, the box and slice balance identities of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] hold for the total tensor with zero divergence, retaining all side-flux terms. For each component $b$ and $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, set $\mathcal F^b(s_1,s_2):=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\left(\int_{[s_1,s_2]	imes K_i^+}T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]	imes K_i^-}T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{ib}\,d^3xight)$, with $K:=\prod_{i=1}^{3}[c_i,d_i]$, its faces $K_i^\pm$, and $Q^b(s):=\int_K T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$ as in that theorem. Then $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=-\mathcal F^b(s_1,s_2)$, so $Q^b(s_2)=Q^b(s_1)$ if and only if $\mathcal F^b(s_1,s_2)=0$. In particular, $Q^b$ is constant throughout $[c_0,d_0]$ if and only if this net signed side flux vanishes on every subinterval $[s_1,s_2]$. The theorem's facewise-zero side-flux hypothesis is sufficient, but is not necessary, for constancy; zero divergence alone does not guarantee it. The angular current $M^{\lambda\mu
u}:=x^\mu T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda
u}-x^
u T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\mu}$ satisfies $\partial_\lambda M^{\lambda\mu
u}=0$ by symmetry. (e) [Scope] the divergence is a product identity of $C^1$ objects and is not asserted for the weak branch, at singular source support or for any product of distributions; symmetry, zero trace and the component display are algebraic; no matter tensor is derived from vacuum Maxwell, no radiation reaction or self-force is included, and no empirical claim is made.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct algebra from the components for (a)-(b); the product rule and the cyclic identity for (c); summation and the finite-box theorem for (d). (a) Symmetry: $\eta_{\alpha eta}F^{\mu\alpha}F^{
u eta}=\eta_{\alpha eta}F^{\mu eta}F^{
u\alpha}$ by relabelling, and $\eta^{\mu
u}$ is symmetric; trace: $\eta_{\mu
u}T^{\mu
u}=\mu_0^{-1}(F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta}-	frac14\cdot4\cdot F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta})=0$; the transformation law is contraction of two copies of the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii) with $\eta$ invariant, and the regularity is the component criterion of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] (every term is a polynomial in the $C^1$ components). (b) Substituting $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and $F^{00}=0$: $T^{00}=\mu_0^{-1}(|E|^2/c^2+	frac14\cdot2(|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2))=\varepsilon_0|E|^2/2+|B|^2/(2\mu_0)$ using $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$; $T^{0i}=\mu_0^{-1}F^{0j}F^i{}_j=(E	imes B)_i/(\mu_0c)$ with [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; $T^{ij}=-\sigma_{ij}$ by the component computation $\sum_k\epsilon_{ikm}\epsilon_{jkn}B_mB_n=\delta_{ij}|B|^2-B_iB_j$ and the negative temporal contraction of $F^{i0}F^{j}{}_0$. (c) Product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\mu_0\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}=(\partial_\mu F^{\mu\alpha})F^
u{}_\alpha+F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F^
u{}_\alpha-	frac12F^{\alpha eta}\partial^
u F_{\alpha eta}$; the first factor is $-\mu_0j^\alpha$ by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] ((TM1)), giving $-f^
u$; for the cancellation set $I=F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta}$ and fix a free index $\kappa$. Contract the cyclic identity $\partial_\mu F_{\kappa\alpha}+\partial_\kappa F_{\alpha\mu}+\partial_\alpha F_{\mu\kappa}=0$ with $F^{\mu\alpha}$. Its first and third terms both equal $C_\kappa:=F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F_{\kappa\alpha}$, the third by interchanging the dummy indices and using alternation twice; the middle term is $-F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\kappa F_{\mu\alpha}=-	frac12\partial_\kappa I$. Hence $C_\kappa=	frac14\partial_\kappa I$. Raise only this free index: $F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F^
u{}_\alpha=	frac14\partial^
u I=	frac12F^{\alpha eta}\partial^
u F_{\alpha eta}$, so the two product-rule terms cancel. The first term is $-\mu_0 j^\alpha F^
u{}_\alpha=-\mu_0 F^{
u\lambda}j_\lambda$, giving precisely $-f^
u$ after dividing by $\mu_0$. All repeated indices here are dummy indices and the free index is never reused in $I$. The component identities are (b) read in $(c)$; they coincide with the independently proved local identities of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a) and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (a). (d) Add the matter equation; the finite box and slice balance identities, with side flux retained, are [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] applied to the $C^1$ symmetric total tensor with vanishing divergence; the angular identity uses $\partial_\lambda x^\mu=\delta^\mu_\lambda$ and the symmetry $T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\mu
u}=T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{
u\mu}$. The algebra gives $f^0=J\cdot E/c$ and $f^i=ho E_i+(J	imes B)_i$; identifying those source terms with matter work and force uses [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (ii) only in that interpretation. (e) records the regularity scope. No choice principle and no empirical premise are used.

Excluded: the weak branch, singular support, products of distributions, any derivation of a matter tensor from vacuum Maxwell, radiation reaction, self-force and any empirical claim.

items.title: Boosted uniform electric field and the mixed magnetic field
items.statement: Let $E_0>0$ carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and consider the constant fields of [[def-em-fields]] $$E:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3,\quad E\equiv E_0e_2,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ which form a source-free smooth solution of the vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (all first derivatives vanish and $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}B=0$). Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the boosted inertial chart of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]]. Then the components of the same field in $x'$ are $$E'=\gamma E_0\,e_2,\qquad B'=-\frac{\gamma\beta E_0}{c}\,e_3=-\frac{\gamma |v|E_0}{c^2}\,e_3,$$ so the moving observer reads an electric field of magnitude $\gamma E_0$ along $e_2$ and, for $\beta>0$, a nonzero magnetic field along $-e_3$: a purely electric uniform field acquires a magnetic component in the boosted description. The two invariants check directly: with the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=\gamma^2\Bigl(\frac{\beta^2E_0^2}{c^2}-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}\Bigr)=-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=0=E\cdot B,$$ using $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]). At $\beta=0$ the formulas reduce to $E'=E$, $B'=0$. The computation is exact for the constant field; the example reports no measurement, identifies no source producing the field, and asserts nothing about finite-energy or bounded configurations.
items.strategy: **Verification:** substitute the data into clause (a) of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] with $\beta$ as given. Here $E_\parallel=0$, $B_\parallel=0$ since $E\perp e_1$ and $B=0$, and $v\times B=0$, while $v\times E=(\beta c e_1)\times(E_0e_2)=\beta cE_0e_3$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the boost formulas give $E'=\gamma E_0e_2$ and $B'=-\gamma |v|E_0e_3/c^2=-\gamma\beta E_0e_3/c$. The invariant values are computed with [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the identity $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]; the constant field is a solution of the source-free smooth branch because every displayed first derivative vanishes. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.
items.physical_scope: An exact algebraic example for one uniform static electric field ($E\equiv E_0e_2$, $B\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $E_0>0$ in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) and one passive boost along $e_1$ with $0\le\beta<1$: the boosted components, the resulting mixed magnetic field and the two field invariants. Excluded: real sources of the uniform field, boundary or finite-support configurations, measurements and any empirical claim.
